articles.title: The Valkyries gave Gabby Williams the keys. She turned an expansion team into a Bay Area phenomenon
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO — Veronica Burton, flying solo, enjoyed a meal at the bar of Michael Jordan's restaurant at the Mohegan Sun in Connecticut. A stranger approach...
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — Veronica Burton, flying solo, enjoyed a meal at the bar of Michael Jordan's restaurant at the Mohegan Sun in Connecticut. A stranger approached, starstruck, declaring to be a huge fan.

Burton would've responded kindly even if she didn't feel like being bothered. But she kind of liked the excitement her presence created. So she obliged the admirer. A little conversation. A photograph together. The generous fan even picked up the tab on her dinner.

"I was like, 'Oh my gosh. Thank you,'" Burton said, drumming up the same surprising look on her face she flashed back then.

The whole experience moved the typically low-key Burton. And at the end of this heartwarming exchange, the Valkyries point guard got a humbling reminder how the world she inhabits belongs to Gabby Williams.

"And as they were leaving," Burton said, already breaking into a laugh, "they were like, 'OK, bye, Gabby. Thank you.'"

Burton faced a dilemma. Correct the mistaken identity? Or let the stranger leave with a cherished memory. She'd received a free meal and adoration courtesy of her teammate. So she chose the latter. Somewhere, a fan perhaps treasures a photograph with a woman they believe is Gabby Williams.

The Valkyries stars still laugh about this. Such is the celebrity of the Valkyries' hometown star.

"They can't tell mixed people apart," Williams said laughing, simultaneously deflecting the magnitude of her stardom.

For years, Williams carried a conviction the WNBA had yet to validate. A franchise player lived somewhere beneath the established defensive brilliance, the versatility that made her indispensable to every team, the selflessness that made her valuable to her team's culture. The league had yet to see her as a cornerstone. But she believed. The player who'd put France on her back, who for years overseas had been entrusted with the biggest moments, could be the face of a franchise in the WNBA.

She just needed the freedom to emerge. A kingdom willing to hand her the keys. She'd done everything else in her seven-year career. Defensive specialist. Starter with a defined role. Game-changing reserve. A role player who could fill in for the star in short windows. But never the one around whom everything revolved.

And despite all her contributions, the endings rarely changed. Her team still went home too early. She made it out of the first round once, in 2022, before this season.

So when free agency arrived, Williams decided she was done following the familiar script. At 29, and emboldened by the 2024 Olympics where she led France to a near upset of the United States, she listened to the voice in her head. The one insisting she belonged among the elite. The one whispering, "Tell me when to go," while awaiting the opportunity to produce proof.

She chose an expansion franchise, betting that a team with no history could become the stage for the greatest chapter of her own. And of all the places for her prophecy to find its fulfillment, it happened at home.

In the Bay Area, where childhood memories still linger — from her cousin's house in East Oakland to running around Pier 39 after youth basketball tournaments — Williams found the belief she'd been seeking. The Golden State Valkyries handed her the keys. She gave them a star and took them the WNBA Finals .

Now the same region that helped raise her proudly elevates her as one of its beloved icons. Williams understands the spirit here, the energy that's turned Chase Center into one of the WNBA's most daunting venues. She recognizes the diversity of the audience, the eclectic swag and progressive passion, where urban swag melds with corporate culture because everybody here blows the whistle.

The girl who dreamed to meet the stars she admired has become one they want to meet. The young hooper who once longed to see someone who looked like her representing her home team has become that very figure for another generation. A childhood wish fulfilled by a grown woman's audacity to believe in herself.

"I don't even have the words for it, honestly," Williams said. "Growing up here and knowing what this community is about, and seeing it at this level means everything. Like, the Bay has always been love. The Bay's always been a community like this. And now all these people that have been Bay Area legends that I've looked up to since I was a kid … it just feels like a big party. And I'm just enjoying it, honestly, I'm enjoying it. I'm taking advantage of it, taking advantage of this energy and this magic that we have in this arena."

The line snaked across the parking lot of Trader Joe's. A sea of violet bubbling with anticipation to see the Bay Area's newest superstar. Fans clutched gifts to give her. Some bearing tributes to her love of anime. Others honoring her affection for cats. All hoping for a few seconds with the woman who'd become the ambassador of a movement.

Williams showed up for a routine meet-and-greet at Peet's Coffee on Lakeshore Avenue in Oakland. An hour of handshakes, photographs and signatures. The kind of obligation that comes with being the centerpiece of a professional sports franchise.

Except nothing about the reception waiting for her qualified as routine.

The crowd had overwhelmed the parking lot. Chants of "Gabby! Gabby!" rang out on this busy street. So many fans she didn't come close to greeting all of them. It was the kind of turnout reserved for celebrities accustomed to being mobbed.

Williams was still getting used to being one of those. "I think that was really a turning point of her understanding of how deeply the Bay felt connected to her," Jess Smith, the Valkyries' president of business operations, said.

For all her confidence between the lines, Williams possesses little of the self-importance often associated with stardom. Her game is loud. Her personality, comparatively, is quiet. She can suffocate an opposing superstar with her defense, seize command of a fourth quarter, then seem almost embarrassed when thousands of people chant her name.

"She almost gets uncomfortable when people are hyping her up," Burton said. "But I think it's been really cool to see her personality just thrive here."

The contradiction is part of her appeal. The relentless competitor who doesn't seem particularly interested in the trappings of celebrity. The player who believed she could be the face of a franchise but never appeared consumed with being the center of attention.

Williams concedes the adoration requires adjustment. "I'm not someone who's going to ask for attention," she said.

Sometimes, she wonders why her. What makes her worthy of this kind of love?

But it's the part that comes with what she wanted. Being on top means accepting the gifts and the burdens. She's learned to see the affection as something beyond popularity. But a responsibility.

"I would have loved to have had a role model who looked like me playing for my home team in the Bay Area," Williams said.

That awareness informs how she treats people. Why she gives fans her undivided attention, making each interaction feel personal rather than obligatory. Her willingness to be herself is precisely what makes her so magnetic.

"She makes everyone feel seen," Smith said. "She makes everyone feel welcome. When you have an interaction with her, it's just 100 percent."

The setting also fit the figure. This wasn't a velvet-roped nightclub or an exclusive celebrity gathering. This was a neighborhood coffee shop in Oakland. A place where the distance between an adored athlete and the people who adore her can shrink to a conversation, a photograph, a shared laugh. In this case, an impromptu rally across the street from Chipotle, next to a wings spot called Proposition Chicken.

That's what the Valkyries gave Williams. The freedom to become a star.

What's been overwhelming is the size and fervor of this kingdom she now governs. The Valkyries are a beacon for the Bay Area's love affair with women's basketball, a relationship fulfilled mostly by Stanford for decades with a few moments by Cal sprinkled in. But it's real. It's intense.

Williams was driving on some random stretch of highway she didn't even remember. A place she never expected the Valkyries' fervor to reach. But as she drove, an overpass let her know just how lit this area is about the Valkyries. It was Valkyries Day — Sept. 25, 2026 — as decreed by San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie.

"I was near Daly City, pretty far, and I had a long drive back to Oakland," Williams said. "This is far from Chase Center. This is far from Oakland. …. And there's like 50 people on a bridge just shouting at cars, in Valkyries gear. It's not a game day. They have signs and all the cars are honking and stuff. And I was like, 'Oh my gosh.' I think I really realized then just what a big deal the Valkyries were to this community."

That realization gave her the confidence for one of the moments that will forever be remembered on this Valkyries run to the finals, where they'll face the Atlanta Dream.

Williams had already given the Chase Center crowd plenty to cheer about in beating the Dallas Wings in Game 1 of their first-round series. But this night held something extra.

The Bay Area rap legend performed at halftime, and Ballhalla blew the whistle. For Williams, whose childhood soundtrack included plenty of his music, the presence of Too $hort was almost as exciting as the playoff victory.

So in her postgame interview on the court with USA Network, she couldn't resist taking a risk.

"I heard Too $hort was in the building," Williams announced. "I couldn't lose in front of Too $hort."

Then, spontaneously, she decided to test the cultural fluency of thousands of people. More than that, she decided to test how much she had the heart of Valkyries fans.

Would they follow her down this road? Would they understand?

"I told (Laeticia Amihere)," Williams recalled, laughing, "I was like, if nobody said anything, I would have never shown my face in that arena ever again."

She was nervous. But she believed in their connection, in the bond they'd built. They understood her. She understood. This Bay Area love, between Williams and the Valkyries, was real. She would prove it with a question for the 18,000 fans.

The response was thunderous. Because this is Gabby's world. Her prophecy is fulfilled.

articles.title: New NBA Rumors Reveal Why Warriors Didn't Seriously Pursue Anthony Davis, Jaylen Brown Trades
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors weren't willing to offer Jimmy Butler and the draft capital required to trade for Anthony Davis or Jaylen Brown during the 2026 offseason, according to ESPN's Anthony Slater.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors weren't willing to offer Jimmy Butler and the draft capital required to trade for Anthony Davis or Jaylen Brown during the 2026 offseason, according to ESPN's Anthony Slater .

"The Warriors didn't show an appetite to offer Butler for Anthony Davis or Jaylen Brown this summer, considering the pick packages required and contracts attached to both," Slater reported Friday. "All other Butler-plus-picks conversations -- for what the Warriors believe are ultimately lesser players once Butler returns -- were shut down, team sources said."

ESPN's Shams Charania previously reported that the Warriors planned to pursue LeBron James in free agency and Davis on the trade market, pairing them alongside Stephen Curry.

James ultimately signed with the Philadelphia 76ers while Davis stayed put with the Washington Wizards.

The Warriors also could have entered the mix for Brown before deciding not to give up a package that contained roughly four first-round picks, per Charania .

Brown also landed in Philadelphia, as the Boston Celtics traded him to the 76ers on July 1.

The inclusion of Butler also appeared to be a sticking point in discussions involving Davis and Brown. Butler suffered a torn ACL on Jan. 19.

The six-time All-Star has been a key piece of the Warriors' starting lineup when healthy, averaging 19.1 points, 5.5 rebounds and 5.3 assists per game while shooting 50.1 percent from the field across his two seasons with the organization.

Golden State primarily focused on retaining its own players during the summer, as the team's only external additions were Georges Niang and Brandon Williams.

articles.title: WNBA Finals tickets: Golden State Valkyries-Atlanta Dream matchup setting records ahead of Game 1
articles.summary: As the WNBA reaches a crescendo to its historic 30th season, the 2026 WNBA Finals get underway on Saturday with Game 1 at Chase Center in the Bay Area.
articles.body:
As the WNBA reaches a crescendo to its historic 30th season, the 2026 WNBA Finals get underway on Saturday with Game 1 at Chase Center in the Bay Area. With the Golden State Valkyries in the Finals in only their second year in existence, "Ballhalla" will be rocking for the matchup with the Atlanta Dream, if ticket sales are any indication.

Get-in prices for Games 1 and 2 in San Francisco have hovered around $200 a ticket, according to Gametime . That's well above the previous record from last year: per Gametime, one day out from Game 1 of the Finals between the Phoenix Mercury and Las Vegas Aces, the get-in price was $48. On Friday, the get-in for this weekend's Game 1 was $204.

It's no huge surprise that Games 1 and 2 at Chase Center are setting records, since the Valkyries have done that ever since they entered the league as an expansion team last year, selling out every home game at the 18,000-seat arena. They led the league in both average and total attendance in 2026.

The Dream, meanwhile, had their Finals Games 3 and 4 moved to State Farm Arena (capacity 17,000) after the team, WNBA and NBA came together to resolve conflicts that would've forced them to play at their usual home, Gateway Center Arena (capacity 3,500). The Dream will officially move to State Farm Arena for the 2027 season, and had played all their first-round and semifinal games at the larger venue.

Tickets for Games 3 and 4 in Atlanta are $85 and $95, respectively, to get in the door. Game 3, on Wednesday, Oct. 21, was moved up one day because of a concert at State Farm, while Game 4, on Saturday, Oct. 24, was moved up a few hours with the Atlanta Hawks opening their home slate against the Houston Rockets later that night. A plan for a potential Game 6, which would conflict with another Hawks home game, was not announced.

articles.title: Internet owes Panthers forward Brady Tkachuk big apology after second consecutive hat trick
articles.summary: Brady Tkachuk notched back-to-back hat tricks for the Florida Panthers after a scoreless start, becoming the first to do so since Auston Matthews in 2024.
articles.body: When the Florida Panthers acquired forward Brady Tkachuk in a trade with the Ottawa Senators over the summer, hockey fans and pundits everywhere bemoaned the fact that an already established champion was slowly becoming a super team. And who could blame them? After all, the Cats were coming off of winning back-to-back Stanley Cups just 12 months earlier, and the only reason they missed the playoffs in 2026 was due in large part to a historic rash of injuries to some of their biggest stars. Adding Tkachuk seemed like a case of the rich getting richer, as Florida recovered to full strength while adding one of the best young players in the game to their roster. For the first couple weeks of the season, it looked like the addition of Matthew's younger brother was all smoke and mirrors, with Brady being held to zero points through the first five games of the year. Rival fans were quick to jump all over this fact, given that both the Panthers and the Tkachuk brothers were seen as polarizing villains throughout the NHL. The internet had a field day, but just as the fans started to take their victory laps, Brady got hot. Then he became nuclear. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE After breaking the points seal three games prior with an assist in a 5-3 loss in Buffalo, the younger Tkachuk brother notched back-to-back hat tricks in wins over Columbus on Tuesday and Vancouver on Thursday, becoming the first to do so since fellow American Auston Matthews in 2024. His three goals against the Canucks proved to be the difference, too, as the Cats needed every bit of Brady's offensive prowess to squeak out a 3-2 victory in overtime. Matthew became the first player in NHL history to assist his brother on all three goals of a natural hat trick. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER In short, the Tkachuk brothers are on fire, and if they can carry the water for Florida - along with other Panthers like Sam Bennett, Sam Reinhart, and Seth Jones - while Brad Marchand and captain Aleksander Barkov are out with injuries, the Cats could be a dangerous team heading into the new year. There's still almost a full season of hockey to play, but there are plenty of Eastern Conference teams who will be looking under their beds at night now that Florida seems to have their mojo back.

articles.title: Philly gay sports bar canceled by its own for not being gay enough on eve of WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Marsha's South Street, a Philly gay sports bar, will close after LGBTQIA+ community accusations of transphobia, misogyny and microaggressions.
articles.body: A Philly gay sports bar will close its doors this weekend after members of the LGBTQIA+ community accused it of a cocktail of egregious behavior, including transphobia, misogyny and a slew of microaggressions. With Game 1 of the WNBA Finals set for Saturday afternoon, instead of a celebration of everything queer, Marsha's South Street will hold its own funeral. After facing serious allegations of the bar not being gay enough, Black queer bar owner Chivonn Anderson tried to hold on for dear life, but ultimately she was left no choice but to call it quits during the Holy Grail for gay sports bars. "It is with heavy hearts that we have decided to close Marsha’s doors for good. We have loved serving this community, and still believe that more than ever this city needs more women/queer/BIPOC- owned businesses," Anderson wrote Thursday on the bar's Instagram page. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "For all of our beloved regulars and supporters- we will miss you! Please come by this weekend and say goodbye. We will be open Friday, Saturday, and Sunday for one last hurrah before we shut down," she added. How is it possible for a Philly gay sports bar not to be gay enough? This all started back in April when Black trans manager and bartender Olivia Rhodes claimed that the place was a hellhole for gays to work. "Marsha’s may claim to be a queer safe space, but it is nothing like that," Rhodes said on Instagram. It was the ultimate insult. Word quickly got around. Fair or not, Marsha's was in trouble. Rhodes also claimed the bar's general manager, Rylan, said that nonbinary queers were "overly emotional, too sensitive" and that the place needed to hire more men because the bar could use "more testosterone." You get the point. The workers wanted this place to be way gayer. More trans. "Marsha's has a long history of misogyny, and racism that doesn't align with the queer identity it claims and represents," Rhodes charged. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! Another former worker, who is a biracial, bisexual woman, claimed she was treated poorly, too. There were also allegations levied on Reddit by an employee who says the head chef misgendered workers. "Marsha's is actively and explicitly not a queer space, it's at BEST a space for cis white lesbians to come ogle the 3-4 minorities that come through on any given night and at worst it's just a straight sports bar half-heartedly marketed as vaguely lesbian adjacent," a Reddit user added. Anderson tried her best to weather the storm. She even bent the knee in a September Instagram post that was clearly a full-court shot to save her business as the WNBA playoffs were firing on all cylinders. "We have trained staff on biased language and microaggressions," the bar owner wrote. "We enforce a zero-tolerance policy against hate and bias. We have worked with, and will continue to work with, amazing restorative justice practitioners in our community that have held us accountable. We have done the work, and we want to keep growing." Too late. The gays already canceled you, Chivonn. Now you're hosting a funeral as Angel Reese tips off her first WNBA Finals. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD "It must be liquidated," the angry Reddit user wrote in April of the bar. Mission accomplished.

articles.title: Vidorreta explica el no fichaje de Sima: "No me dieron la opción de llamarle para convencerle"
articles.standfirst: El excajista no volverá al Carpena
articles.summary: El excajista no volverá al Carpena
articles.body: El técnico del Unicaja apunta a la reacción del entorno del jugador como una posible explicación de su negativa a regresar a Málaga y reconoce que el equipo sigue buscando refuerzos para el juego interior. Txus Vidorreta ha abordado uno de los asuntos pendientes del mercado del Unicaja en la previa del encuentro ante el Kids&Us Manresa: la posibilidad frustrada de incorporar a Yankuba Sima. El técnico cajista ha reconocido que le habría gustado contar con el pívot, aunque ha deslizado que la reacción que generó su nombre pudo influir en la decisión del jugador de no regresar a Málaga. "A nosotros se nos transmite que él no contempla volver a Málaga", ha explicado Vidorreta, que ha apuntado a la respuesta del entorno del jugador cuando surgió la opción de su fichaje. "¿Cuál fue la reacción cuando salió el nombre de Sima? Yo no tengo redes, pero algo me han contado. Tibieza. Eso no nos ha ayudado", ha señalado. El entrenador vasco considera que esa reacción pudo afectar al jugador, aunque ha dejado claro que se trata de una hipótesis. "Me da la sensación de que a él sí le ha afectado. Insisto en que es una hipótesis", ha matizado antes de reivindicar la importancia que tuvo Sima en su anterior etapa en el club. "Para mí era un jugador muy importante al que ojalá hubiéramos podido fichar. No me dieron la opción de llamarle para convencerle", ha lamentado. El Unicaja sigue buscando refuerzos interiores La salida de Sima deja al Unicaja sin una incorporación que habría ayudado a aliviar sus problemas en la pintura. Vidorreta ha confirmado que el club continúa trabajando en el mercado para completar una rotación interior que considera insuficiente. "Tenemos ahora tres pívots en el equipo: Noua, Willy y Kravish", ha explicado el técnico, que también ha detallado los ajustes que está realizando para compensar las bajas. Sima está siendo reconvertido al puesto de cuatro, mientras que Barreiro está actuando exclusivamente en esa posición. "No hemos podido completar ese cinco que nos falta. En estos momentos estamos en el mercado, pero sabéis las dificultades que hay", ha reconocido Vidorreta, que incluso ha abierto la puerta a incorporar más de un jugador. "Si podemos sumar dos jugadores, mejor que uno, pero primero hay que encontrar uno. Si es un cuatro y medio, nos resuelve dos problemas".

articles.title: Fantasy Basketball: 6 last-minute tips to help you nail your drafts
articles.summary: Dan Titus offers some tips for your fantasy basketball draft heading into the final weekend before the regular season.
articles.body:
The NBA season starts next Tuesday, and if you're like me, you will be knocking out your final fantasy basketball drafts this weekend. Here are six tips to help you cram last minute and dominate your drafts!

Check out my free fantasy basketball draft kit!

Rankings aren't one-size-fits-all, but like average draft position, they are another data point that can help fantasy managers come draft time. It's impossible to predict the correct outcome for every player. However, you can get a feel for which players are higher or lower than the ADP. If I'm higher on a player, I've likely mentioned them in my sleeper, breakout or fade articles. Get all of those, plus my rankings by format, in the 2026-27 fantasy basketball draft kit .

If you want more, the Fantasy Ultra Playbook is a comprehensive resource that'll provide additional insight into my draft strategies, player projections and more for the upcoming season.

Want to know where players are being drafted? The Draft Analysis tool is the easiest and best way to do so. By evaluating a player's Average Draft Position (ADP), Yahoo analyzes the market across its draft platform to show when players are selected. ADP is a valuable data point when building a fantasy team because you'll want to base decisions on the latest market trends. Which, at times, may be viewed as an overcorrection (an opportunity to capitalize on falling value) or a reaction to new information (such as the Warriors managing Stephen Curry's workload ).

Pulling the ADP thread some more, mock drafting helps you understand how to adapt during positional runs and how the market may view a player as you approach your drafts. With preseason in full swing and news dropping daily, things change quickly. If you get your draft position early, practice selecting the players you want to build your team around. Have contingencies in case you get sniped. If you don't have a draft position until 45 minutes before you draft, then try mocking from different draft slots to get a feel for each part of the draft. It's very helpful and there's a reason why analysts are constantly mocking — its's not just for content. Knowing what'll be available and where to reach or pivot is key to gaining an edge in your drafts.

Turn on Twitter/X notifications for top NBA reporters

NBA insiders like Shams Charania , Jake Fischer and Chris Haynes are worth following for the latest news that may impact your fantasy basketball draft. From injuries to player absences, projected starting lineups and more, it's critical to understand the latest news so you can go into drafts with the most up-to-date information possible. For fantasy, Rotowire NBA and UnderdogNBA are the most reliable news aggregators for tracking how the insider information might affect your fantasy teams.

I prefer to evaluate players on per-game value rather than total value because injuries are, unfortunately, part of fantasy basketball. Players like Mikal Bridges often rank higher in head-to-head formats because their availability is a valuable asset. Using Bridges as an example, he finished 16th in total value last season, but if you look under the hood, he finished 40th in per-game value. So he got a significant boost by simply playing more games.

On the flip side, Stephen Curry finished ninth in per-game value a season ago, versus 88th in total value. When Curry played, he was a top-10 player. The problem was that he played only 43 games. With Warriors head coach Steve Kerr admitting Curry will be load-managed this year, Curry's per-game value inflates his current ADP. We know who Curry is; he's one of the greatest players (and fantasy players) of all time. Fantasy basketball often comes down to balancing ceiling outcomes and variance.

Just because someone might get hurt doesn't mean you shouldn't draft them. The per-game output gives a better read on how impactful they can be. Total value is a reliability factor that still matters, but per-game is the stronger signal. Basketball Monster is a great resource that lets you toggle between per-game and total values from last season.

Evaluating player breakouts using betting markets

Are you wondering who might be last season's Amen Thompson, Keyonte George or Nickeil Alexander-Walker? Or who makes the All-Star leap? Well, I often use betting markets to determine those candidates. Evaluating player award markets and their odds of winning provides another data point. The markets I'd be most interested in are Most Improved Player, MVP, Rookie of the Year and Defensive Player of the Year. There are also prop markets for most points scored, most assists, most rebounds and more.

It may seem trivial, but I'm confident you'll see several of the names listed for those markets emerge as viable candidates to win their respective awards and be valuable fantasy assets this year.

Mock drafts are one thing, but the players I keep coming back to tell a better story about how I'm approaching this season. Here are the guys I've drafted most often, whether it's because of their value, upside or how well they fit my preferred roster builds. For more analysis on the players listed below, check out my All-Breakout team and favorite pick in each round of a 12-team league .

articles.title: Kevin Garnett's NSFW reaction to Timberwolves jersey retirement will leave you creasing
articles.summary: Nearly two decades after being sent to the Celtics — and one decade after retiring from the sport — Kevin Garnett is finally receiving his flowers from the T...
articles.body:
Kevin Garnett finally will get the chance to see his Timberwolves jersey leap to the rafters this season. He likely wouldn't have envisioned it taking the franchise a decade to do so when he first skipped town.

Garnett spent 14 years cloaked in Minnesota colors. Conventional wisdom would suggest that the Timberwolves would have worked quick to celebrate their greatest-ever player, who was inducted into the Basketball Hall of Fame in 2020.

That didn't quite come to fruition, though. Now, nearly two decades after he was shipped off to the Celtics and a decade after he retired, Garnett is finally receiving the flowers from the side he is most synonymous with. Suffice to say, Garnett isn't holding back his thoughts on how long the wait was.

With that, here's a look at Garnett's reaction — in all its glory — to news of his impending jersey retirement.

Kevin Garnett's NSFW reaction to Timberwolves jersey retirement

Garnett will see his vaunted No. 21 jersey go up in the rafters at Target Center when the Timberwolves host Boston on Feb. 28. He'll become the second player in franchise history to receive the honor, joining former teammate Malik Sealy, whose No. 2 was retired after he died in a car accident in 2000.

Garnett admitted that the honor was a long-time coming on an episode of his "KG Certified" podcast released on Friday.

"They made a m— wait 10 years," Garnett said. "They made a m— wait long enough, b— ass n—."

With respect to Kevin Love, Karl-Anthony Towns and Anthony Edwards, Garnett is by far the greatest player in Minnesota history. He was a three-time first-team All-NBA selection across 14 seasons with the Timberwolves. Garnett's impressive play culminated with a glittering 2003-04 campaign that saw him earn MVP honors after posting averages of 24.2 points, 13.9 rebounds, 5.0 assists, 2.2 blocks and 1.6 steals per game.

Garnett remains the franchise's all-time leader in games (970), points (19,201), rebounds (10,718), assists (4,216), blocks (1,590), steals (1,315) and triple-doubles (16). While Garnett's response to the honor was humorous, the length of time it took for Minnesota to put his No. 21 in the rafters is surprising.

The reason why the Timberwolves took so long to enshrine their greatest-ever player with the franchise's highest honor is simple, though. He just didn't get along with former Minnesota owner Glen Taylor. Garnett and Taylor locked horns following his trade to the Celtics in 2007.

Former Timberwolves president and coach Flip Saunders attempted to mend things in the early 2010s. But things fell apart after Saunders died, leading to another cold war between the two.

Taylor's decision to sell Minnesota appears to have opened the door for Garnett to receive his just rewards for a 14-year career well spent in the Land of 1,000 Lakes. He should get quite the reception when he makes his long-awaited return to the house he helped forge.

articles.title: OKC Thunder call bluff on Spanish club's legal threats over Aday Mara
articles.summary: Oklahoma City Thunder call bluff on Spanish club's legal threats over Aday Mara.
articles.body:
You gotta give Aday Mara's old Spanish club credit — they love some theatrics. Not even a full day after he finished a superb preseason, Basket Zaragoza is threatening to take legal action over the Oklahoma City Thunder and the NBA if he suits up for Opening Night in five days.

Now, how much power do they have in enforcing that? Remains to be seen, but not a lot. Mara played with Basket Zaragoza from 2021-23. Five years later, they apparently still have his playing rights. Never mind the fact that he played for UCLA and Michigan in three collegiate seasons since then.

The Spanish club has reached out to the Thunder, the NBA and FIBA over Mara's status. And from the reactions afterward, it looks like their threats have fallen on deaf ears. I guess we'll see if OKC's play to call its bluff will work out. As of now, expect the 21-year-old to play from the jump.

The Thunder released an official statement — through several NBA reporters — in response to the situation. Here's what they said about the possible legal actions over Mara: "Aday last played three years of NCAA college basketball and therefore, as advised by the NBA, no clearance from the Spanish team is required for him to play in the NBA."

The Thunder added Mara with the No. 12 pick of the 2026 NBA draft. He enjoyed a breakout collegiate season at Michigan. Alongside Yaxel Lendeborg and Morez Johnson Jr., the three-headed frontcourt monster helped the Wolverines win a 2026 national championship.

Do I think the Thunder will oblige the Spanish club's hilariosuly-timed request? No. Probably not. The NCAA didn't when UCLA went through the same song and dance when Mara first moved to the United States. That said, can't deny that this isn't the type of distraction you need if you're hoping to be a title contender.

It hasn't taken long for Mara to tease his NBA potential on the Thunder. He was arguably one of the biggest impact players throughout the preseason. On both ends of the floor, too. To the point that you have to wonder if the 7-foot-3 giant can help OKC as soon as the first day of the 2026-27 regular season.

articles.title: El Barça roza la hazaña ante el campeón antes de caer en la prórroga
articles.standfirst: Remontó 14 puntos en el último cuarto para llevar al límite al Olympiacos
articles.summary: Remontó 14 puntos en el último cuarto para llevar al límite al Olympiacos
articles.body: El Barcelona rozó la proeza de ganar al campeón de Europa. Como el Valencia dos días antes cayó en la prórroga, 100-105, ero a diferencia del Valencia, fue el equipo de Sekulic el que fue de menos a más a lo largo del partido para forzar el tiempo extra. Pero como los taronja no pudieron con los griegos en esos cinco minutos extra que dominaron Montero y Ndiaye. El Olympiacos llegó a tener una máxima de 14 puntos, 60-74, a poco más de un minuto para entregar el tercer acto. Y con tres minutos jugados del cuatro, la ventaja era importante, 70-81 y la sensación era la de que el equipo heleno tenía el choque controlado. Nada de eso, el Barça llegó desde atrás para llevar al campeón al límite. Con un Fournier fallón y un Vezenkov menos activo que en la primera parte (16 puntos sin fallo llevaba al descanso), el Barça fue recortando entre las canastas de Parra, Robinson y Gibson y los rebotes de ataque: el Barça llegó a capturar 20 por 25 en defensa. Un triple de Justin Robinson con Donta Hall encima, que se quedó con él en el cambio, envió el partido a la prórroga con 92-92. Lo extraño fue que, con 89-92 tras un tiro libre de Vezenkov, el Olympiacos permitiera el tiro y no hiciera la falta. Robinson castigó el error. Pero el campeón de la Euroliga demostró que es uno de los equipos que mejor sabe jugar los tiempos extra. Con Ndiaye sobresaliendo, un triple, un mate, un tapón, todo seguido, y Montero dirigiendo las operaciones y apareciendo al final, el Olympiacos se llevó un partido que tuvo que recuperar en el primer cuarto (30-22), que tuvo muy cerca al descanso (47-57), que controlaba al final del tercer cuarto pero que tuvo que ganar de nuevo en cinco minutos de añadido. Vezenkov acabó como el mejor anotador del partido, 25 y 38 de valoración. Dio un clinic en más de medio partido pero acabó algo escondido al final. Ndiaye acabó con 17 puntos y 7 rebotes y Montero, mal en la anotación, 13, pero con 1/6 en tiros de dos y 3/5 en triples, estuvo formidable en el pase, 7 asistencias y su +/- fue de +23. En el Barça, Tyrese Martin, en su mejor partido en la Euroliga, se fue a los 17 puntos, los mismos que Robinson. Gibson hizo 11 con 7 asistencias mientras Brizuela se fue hasta los 13 y Nebo acabó con un doble-doble de 11 puntos y 10 rebotes. Para Sekulic, aunque dijo al final del partido que queda muchas cosas por hacer bien, son buenas noticias que muchos jugadores sigan aportando, a pesar por ejemplo del mal partido de Punter (4 puntos y 2/10 en tiros de campo). La mejoría en el rebote (era el peor equipo de la Euroliga en este aspecto), que les dio vida ante Olympiacos es otro de los puntos más destacables de este partido en el que rozaron la hazaña.

articles.title: Mat Ishbia Pledges Suns Will Make NBA Playoffs, Win a Series After Getting Swept by Thunder
articles.summary: Phoenix Suns owner Mat Ishbia says he has faith his team as a playoff contender despite watching them get swept from the first round of the 2025 postseason.
articles.body:
Phoenix Suns owner Mat Ishbia says he has faith his team as a playoff contender despite watching them get swept from the first round of the 2025 postseason.

"We're going to be better than we were last year," Ishbia told CNBC's Alex Sherman in a Thursday appearance on CNBC Sport.

Ishbia continued, "We're going to make the playoffs. We're going to win the first playoff series... We're an ascending young team getting better every day."

Phoenix hasn't won a playoff game since 2023. The Suns were swept by the Minnesota Timberwolves in 2024, missed the postseason altogether in 2025 and were swept again last spring by the Oklahoma City Thunder.

The Suns made it clear the franchise still sees itself as a win-now team by sending out an unprotected first-round pick in order to acquire Miles Bridges from the Charlotte Hornets this summer.

Phoenix now does not hold a first-round pick free of any protection or swap conditions until 2032.

The Suns also sent out Grayson Allen and Royce O'Neale this offseason while adding Luke Kennard and Mark Williams as well as drafting Koa Peat.

Those additions put the Suns on track to boast the third-highest payroll in the NBA this season, per Spotrac .

That is currently projected to put the Suns over the first luxury tax apron. The Suns spent four of the last five seasons as a taxpayer, racking up a $152 million 2025 tax bill before dipping below the limit last season, according to Spotrac .

Given the draft capital and salary the Suns have invested in building a roster around Devin Booker, Jalen Green and Dillon Brooks, the franchise will hope to prove Ishbia's predictions right starting with the tip-off of the regular season next Wednesday a the Portland Trail Blazers.

articles.title: Remontada sin premio del Baskonia en el estreno de Perasovic
articles.standfirst: Iba perdiendo por 17 y llegó a empatar el partido en el último cuarto
articles.summary: Iba perdiendo por 17 y llegó a empatar el partido en el último cuarto
articles.body: La Virtus Bolonia reaccionó a tiempo este viernes ante el nuevo Kosner Baskonia de Velimir Perasovic, que remontó 17 puntos, pero se le apagó la luz en la recta final de la sexta jornada de la Euroliga que acabó con un 86-78. Los vitorianos metieron el miedo en el cuerpo a los italianos en un partido gris en el que se salvó el último cuarto del conjunto del entrenador croata, que empató a 74, pero un 10-0 para los de Álex Mumbrú, liderados por Marcus Carr, dio el cuarto triunfo a los boloñeses. Los italianos entraron mejor en el partido con un parcial 12-0, en el que aprovecharon el tiro libre y el rebote ofensivo para castigar a un Baskonia que comenzó sin energía. Los azulgrana necesitaron cinco minutos para anotar su primera canasta. Los interiores del conjunto italiano castigaron en la pintura vitoriana, con Aliou Diarra como protagonista desde que saltó del banquillo. Las faltas obligaron a Velimir Perasovic a usar a dos 'cuatros' en el juego interior, que tuvo muchos problemas en el rebote en un primer asalto que se cerró con un 24-12 para los locales. Los de Álex Mumbrú marcaron el ritmo y el nivel físico ante un Baskonia que dependía de su inspiración en el uno contra uno y cometió numerosas pérdidas de balón no forzadas. Cada punto de los azulgranas era oro y solo recortaban distancias cuando encadenaban buenas acciones defensivas. Pero, por lo general, los italianos jugaban con relativa comodidad en cada ataque, donde conseguían bandejas a través del uno contra uno, especialmente en el emparejamiento de Marcus Carr. Los porcentajes de los vascos fueron muy bajos y la tercera falta personal de Kenneth Faried puso en problemas al conjunto de Velimir Perasovic, aunque la aportación en el rebote ofensivo de Clement Frisch dio un punto más a los vitorianos. El francés se estrenó en la posición de alero y el Baskonia cambió a pesar de que necesitaba más energía defensiva. El tiro libre permitió a los de Álex Mumbrú mantener una renta cómoda con un 46-34 al descanso. El Baskonia echó en falta a varios jugadores que, hasta la fecha, lideraban las acciones ofensivas, como Chris Duarte y Kenneth Faried. Mientras tanto, la pintura visitante seguía siendo un lugar cómodo para la Virtus, que encontró a Bo Klintman en un buen arranque de los italianos. Las sensaciones y el ritmo del partido volvían a ser para los locales, que estiraron la renta hasta los 17 puntos y encaró el último período con un 68-53. Velimir Perasovic buscó más físico con Tadas Sedekerskis en el puesto de alero y Baskonia pudo situar la diferencia por debajo de los 10 puntos con ocho puntos de Damion Baugh y varias defensas acertadas con protagonismo para Kenneth Faried. El base cambió la cara del Baskonia que igualó el marcador a 74 a menos de cuatro minutos para el final, pero la Virtus reaccionó con 10 puntos clave y un parcial que dejó el choque sentenciado, 86-78. 86 - Virtus Bolonia (24+22+22+18): Carr (20), Moore (12), Alston Jr. (6) Klintman (6) y Diouf (4) -cinco inicial-, Bello (9), Diarra (16), Hackett (7), Frazier (-), Ferrari (3), Kokila (3) y Edwards (-). 78 - Kosner Baskonia (12+22+19+25): Simmons (2), Duarte (2), Stewart (12), Sedekerskis (11) y Faried (6) -cinco inicial-, Kurucs (7), Spagnolo (6), Baugh (8), Frisch (5), Lawson (13) y Santos (6). Árbitros: Milan Nedovic (Eslovenia), Joseph Bissang (Francia) y Uros Obrknezevic (Serbia). Eliminaron por falta personales a Faried (min. 39). Señalaron falta flagrante a Kokila (min. 31). articles.title: Angel Reese Talks Approach Ahead of 1st WNBA Finals, 'The Greats Are Built for This'
articles.summary: Forward Angel Reese is headed to her first-ever WNBA Finals after the Atlanta Dream swept the New York Liberty in the semifinal round. Their Finals matchup with the Golden State Valkyries begins on Saturday afternoon in San Francisco.
articles.body:
Forward Angel Reese is headed to her first-ever WNBA Finals after the Atlanta Dream swept the New York Liberty in the semifinal round. Their Finals matchup with the Golden State Valkyries begins on Saturday afternoon in San Francisco.

Reese appears ready for the moment, per comments made at Finals media day on Friday.

"You have to be a playoff riser," Reese said, per ESPN's Kendra Andrews . "The greats are built for this. If you want to be considered the best player and well respected, you can't shy away from the moment."

Atlanta has met the moment thus far in the playoffs, winning all five of its games after beating the Washington Mystics 2-0 in the first round and the Liberty 3-0 int the semis.

Reese has been beneficial to the Dream's success after Atlanta acquired her from the Chicago Sky last offseason, averaging 16.4 points, a WNBA-high 12.1 rebounds and 1.8 steals per game. She's added 18.0 PPG, 8.4 RPG and 1.6 SPG in five playoff games.

Reese hasn't made the WNBA Finals, but she's won big games and competitions before. In 2023, Reese's LSU Lady Tigers won the NCAA championship to cap a 34-2 season. In September, Reese contributed to Team's USA undefeated campaign in the 2026 World Championships en route to a gold medal.

"Anywhere I go, I am looking to win," Reese said, per Andrews. "I have won at every level I have been at. Coming into any situation, I have a winning mentality -- no matter what it looks like or what it takes."

Game 1 of the best-of-seven series will take place on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET in San Francisco's Chase Center.

articles.title: Defense will win a championship in the 2026 WNBA Finals, but will Valkyries or Dream prevail?
articles.summary: Both the Valkyries and Dream have staked their claims to defense in a year that saw historic offense in the WNBA.
articles.body:
OAKLAND, Calif. — Personally, Kiah Stokes feels validated.

The veteran center crafted a two-time WNBA championship career by being a defensive player. It's fueled her trajectory so much, she's back in the WNBA Finals after averaging 3.6 points per game and less than a bucket over her career.

The No. 2-seeded Golden State Valkyries crushed the league in defensive rating all year (99.1). And amid a season of historic offenses, the gap between the second-year expansion squad and the rest is believed to be the largest of all time.

Standing in their way is the No. 4 Atlanta Dream, the league's second-best defense in 2026, and a team that ratcheted up its tenacity since a trip to Boca Raton during the FIBA World Cup break.

Defense will win a championship this year.

"It is just incredible," Stokes said before practice on Friday at the Valkyries' Sephora Performance Center. "It just shows [that] all those quotes, and now it's like we're just kind of living that moment."

Together, the Valkyries and Dream feature six WNBA All-Defense first- and second-team selections. Dream forward Angel Reese won Defensive Player of the Year. Valkyries forward Gabby Williams finished runner-up. Rhyne Howard (first team) and Jordin Canada (second) joined the 10-player all-defense for Atlanta; Veronica Burton and Stokes for Golden State.

Williams watched the postgame news conferences after the semifinals and noted on Friday before practice that the same cliché was used by their stars — except as a lament, rather than a triumph.

"Like people say, 'defense wins championships,'" New York Liberty veteran Breanna Stewart said of where her team fell short. "It's f***ing true."

The Indiana Fever and Minnesota Lynx set offensive records this season. The Fever averaged 96 points per game and a 115 offensive rating, led by an average of 47 points per game by Kelsey Mitchell and Caitlin Clark. The Lynx paced similarly throughout the season until faltering down the stretch, leading to their Rookie of the Year Olivia Miles finishing second in MVP voting.

Neither team is playing deep into October after their first-round exits to the Aces and Liberty, respectively. It also became the downfall of those Aces and Liberty, who were swept out of the semifinals by the Valkyries and Dream.

"Things get stickier in the playoffs," Williams, an eight-year veteran, said the day before her first WNBA Finals. "For some reason, a lid is going to be on the basket at some point. Things are just tighter, things are more physical, so you can't rely on offense because you can't necessarily control shots going in or not, or getting to the free-throw line, or whatever may be.

"But effort can be controlled way more on the defensive end."

It is where each of these teams has staked their claim to a historic Finals berth, and what they will ride to a first title. The Valkyries are in Year 2 of existence, with team owner Joe Lacob setting a goal of a title in the first five years. The Dream are in their fourth Finals, and first since 2013, but have yet to win since entering the league as an expansion franchise in 2008.

Williams, the Valkyries' signature free-agent signing, later in the conversation rapped her knuckles on the table for luck that shots go in, particularly the last one in a series that could be tight. The Valkyries have made defense the staple since head coach Natalie Nakase, a two-time champion assistant with the Aces, took the job.

"I don't think they wanted to go after any person in the expansion draft, regular draft, or free agency that wasn't going to play defense," Williams said. "I think that starts there."

To lead the league on the defensive side of the ball does not happen by accident. For the Dream, it was a byproduct of a two-year plan by head coach Karl Smesko. He wanted to implement a new offensive identity in his first year on the job after league-lows by the roster. Coming into his second year, he eyed more progress defensively. It super-charged the past two months once play resumed from the international break.

"You always hear that defense wins championships," Howard said. "I don't think that's really been taken into consideration the past years because — not that teams don't play defense, but they're not as defensive-minded as [our teams]. I think it's going to come down really to who can get more stops and who can create easier shots for themselves."

The team that can find more offense could be the one to take individual games in this best-of-seven. It's the second year of the format; last year's series was an Aces sweep of the Mercury. Williams proved herself as the bucket-getter for the Valkyries, though anyone on their roster can pop at different times. The Dream have the better offense, but arguably no bona fide star in her prime that's been on this stage before.

It is the first WNBA Finals since 2021 without either Stewart or Aces five-time MVP A'ja Wilson, and only the third in nine years. They faced each other in two Finals over that span. It is a rare WNBA Finals in that neither team features an MVP candidate. Reese, Howard, Burton and Williams each received a few votes, but none were in true contention.

There is also a lack of individual accomplishment in the coaching category. Neither Smesko nor Nakase won Coach of the Year (Nakase won last year). Janelle Salaün won Sixth Player for a team that received record production off the bench. These are teams of the collective versus the individual.

This Finals series will introduce a superstar proving they're made for the stage. It will almost assuredly come on the defensive side, and it will prove the old adage again — no matter the result.

articles.title: New NBA Rumors on Jaylen Brown-Jayson Tatum Relationship Since Celtics-76ers Blockbuster Trade
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum haven't really spoken since the Boston Celtics traded Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers last July, per ESPN's Malika Andrews (7:45 mark).
articles.body:
Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum haven't really spoken since the Boston Celtics traded Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers last July, per ESPN's Malika Andrews (7:45 mark).

"I was in Philadelphia for media day," Andrews said. "I asked Jaylen Brown whether or not he'd spoken to Jayson Tatum since the exit, and he was a little bit murky, but the essence was: 'No, not really. I went my way and he went his way.'"

The report occurred prior to the Celtics' preseason road game at the Philadelphia 76ers. Boston rested numerous key players (including Tatum). Philadelphia played most of its starters, including Brown.

Brown previously told reporters at his Aug. 6 introductory press conference he and Tatum, who were Celtics teammates from 2017-2026, have "not really" been able to speak since the trade occurred.

Although the two haven't spoken with each other, Brown made it clear during his introductory press conference he respects Tatum

"We won a championship together. Anybody that you win a championship with, you would think that's what a brotherhood or a lifelong legacy would entail," Brown after reporter Bob Manning of CLNS Media Boston Sports Network (h/t Justin Turpin of WEEI) asked him about his relationship with Tatum.

"Obviously, there are ups and downs in any relationship, for sure. But on my end, it's nothing but respect, besides when he plays the Sixers. I hope he does well. But other than that, everything for me is just based in respect."

Tatum made it clear during a Sept. 17 interview on the Dan Patrick Show that he loves Brown.

Although it doesn't appear that Tatum and Brown have spoken much at all since the trade, there aren't any outward signs of animosity or iciness.

Ultimately, the two superstars may have simply moved on. Both have their own responsibilities on Eastern Conference contenders. Brown is on the star-laden 76ers, who also added LeBron James to a team that reached the second round last year. Tatum is the clear alpha now on Boston, which is still trying to remain competitive despite losing Brown. The C's have a host of talents still, including newly acquired Paul George, Payton Pritchard and Derrick White.

The Celtics and 76ers will begin their season series on Nov. 10 in Philadelphia.

articles.title: Tiago Splitter looks forward to ‘loaded’ early Bulls schedule
articles.summary: The Chicago Bulls are itching to get the rebuilding process going. So far, the Bulls are performing decently in the preseason, starting 2-2. They will close...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bulls are itching to get the rebuilding process going. So far, the Bulls are performing decently in the preseason , starting 2-2. They will close out the preseason at home on Friday against the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Then they kick off the regular season on the road against the Toronto Raptors on Wednesday, October 21. After that, the Bulls will have their work cut out for them, as they face formidable opponents from October 21 to November 11.

On October 28 and November 4, Chicago will play the defending champion New York Knicks. Two days later, they will play the Boston Celtics on the road. On November 2 and 8, they will play the Philadelphia 76ers, featuring LeBron James, Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, and VJ Edgecombe. Then, on November 11, the Bulls will play the San Antonio Spurs, featuring Victor Wembanyama.

On paper, that doesn't bode well for a rebuilding team facing some of the league's best talent. However, that didn't sway new head coach Tiago Splitter in the slightest. If anything, he is looking forward to the "loaded" schedule, as he told Sam Smith of NBA.com during the pre-game presser on Friday.

"The beginning of the season is pretty loaded," Splitter said. "But that doesn't change anything."

Splitter is beginning his first season as head coach of the Bulls. They have a mixture of youngsters looking to make it (Caleb Wilson), middle-tier players looking to grow (Matas Buzelis), and veterans looking to lead (Norman Powell, Josh Giddey).

Regardless of who they play, they will be hard to ignore.

articles.title: UCF in Running for 5-Star Recruit Forward RJ Evans
articles.summary: Johnny Dawkins looks to keep local elite talent home as the Knights battle blue-bloods for the son of NBA veteran Reggie Evans in a high-stakes recruiting sh...
articles.body:
UCF Knights men's basketball is in the running for five-star forward RJ Evans, who is prioritizing fit and opportunity before going to the NBA.

Evans is a local product and plays for The Academy of Central Florida. He is a Class of 2029 prospect and has fielded offers from UCF, Louisville, Kentucky and Iowa.

The Knights being among the programs building momentum for the sophomore is promising. Dawkins has landed commitments from high-ranking recruits over his decade-long tenure.

He landed four-star center Moustapha Thiam in 2024 and four-star forward Taylor Hendricks in 2022.

Thiam spent his freshman year with the Knights and averaged 10.4 points, 6.4 rebounds and 2.6 blocks under coach Johnny Dawkins. He improved under Dawkins, but their relationship couldn't hold a candle to the NIL money he received when transferring to Cincinnati.

The Bearcats spent approximately $2 million on Thiam, according to the Orlando Sentinel . Thiam's departure left a sour taste in the mouths of UCF fans, and they let him hear it by booing him in his return to the Addition Financial Arena .

Hendricks became the highest-drafted Knight in 2023. The Utah Jazz drafted him ninth and had a promising rookie season.

He averaged 7.3 points and 4.6 rebounds, alongside nailing 37.9% of his threes. Hendrick's play that year fit the prototypical three-and-D wing that many teams in the league covet.

Evans wants opportunity, and UCF can provide that. Dawkins could prioritize his development over nine months and add him to the long list of Knights drafted in the NBA.

The competition is steep, though. Kentucky and Louisville are top programs in college basketball and routinely develop first-round picks.

Mikel Brown Jr. was the sixth pick by the Brooklyn Nets and scored 15 points in his preseason debut against the Miami Heat .

Prestige and NBA-level development would easily outweigh any influence UCF could have to land a commitment from Evans. He likely knows what NBA-level development is like as the son of former NBA player Reggie Evans.

Reggie Evans had a 13-year career in the NBA as a hard-nosed defender. He was a journeyman and had his best season in 2005-06, averaging 5.6 points while playing for the Seattle SuperSonics and Denver Nuggets .

RJ Evans would be one of UCF's highest-ranked commits if he decides to remain local. Landing high-level recruits is the best way for the program to transform into a perennial NCAA Tournament team.

articles.title: Valkyries-Dream matchup draws a crowd at WNBA Finals media day
articles.summary: Media day for the WNBA Finals was packed as a matchup between Natalie Nakase's Golden State Valkyries and Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream is generating ext...
articles.body:
The Sephora Performance Center was bustling on Friday morning. Any nook or cranny not occupied by the practice courts squished dozens of reporters with notebooks, microphones and television cameras all navigating a train of tables filled with Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries players, ready to talk about the WNBA Finals at media day.

One WNBA official estimated that there would be more media at this Finals than any other the league has hosted in its 30-year existence - perhaps more than the Finals matchup in 2024 between the Minnesota Lynx and New York Liberty as the latter became champions playing in the country's biggest media market.

This says a lot about how far the WNBA has come over the past few years. Finally, the stage is as big and bright as the stakes deserve.

The two teams involved have something to do with the hype, too.

The Valkyries sold out every night at Ballhalla since their inception in 2025 and saw many violet-clad fans follow them on the road as they dominated the league with defense this year.

The Atlanta Dream went big, trading for superstar Angel Reese in the offseason and met the moment, earning their first Finals berth since 2013.

With dozens of microphones pointed and camera lights blaring her way, Reese calmly handed a Chanel purse to a Dream official and sat down with her arms crossed on the table, showing off a tattoo that reads "unapologetic" inked along her right arm.

This is the biggest moment yet for Reese in her young WNBA career, but she's been a star for years. In 2023, she became a central figure in women's basketball when she led Louisiana State University to its first NCAA championship, toppling Caitlin Clark's Iowa Hawkeyes.

She's been thrust under bright lights when her celebration - pointing at her ring finger, gesturing that Clark didn't faze her - became central to a debate that has gripped women's basketball since. She has embraced her celebrity and that conversation.

"I haven't really been able to reflect," Reese said. "I think my journey definitely speaks for itself. I mean, a year ago yesterday, I was walking in Victoria's Secret (fashion show) for the first time ever. Now, a year later, I'm on the biggest stage and being able to be in the Finals."

The attention spreads a little differently on this Valkyries team. Gabby Williams has emerged as the bucket-getter, the best defender on the best defense, and therefore the star for a very popular team.

But Golden State's crew is largely a band of misfits and castoffs who all serve a purpose and whom the Bay Area has learned to love as a collective. The Valkyries' depth may be what wins them the Finals, and it's also what binds them.

With a full week between Game 3 of the semis and Game 1 of the Finals, the Valkyries made sure to enjoy the time between practices. On Thursday, the entire team saw comedian Laura Ramoso at the SF Masonic Auditorium. Ramoso delivers her jokes in Italian, English, French and even a little German - perfect for the multilingual Valkyries.

"I didn't know what to expect, but she was hilarious," forward Kaila Charles said. "She did a lot of European-based jokes because she's half German, half Italian. So it was kind of funny because it reminded me of living overseas, and then (Italian-born Cecilia Zandalasini ) loved it. She did French, everything. So it was a little mix for everybody."

It isn't out of the norm for the Valkyries to hang out with each other off the court. They all hang out at each other's apartments and have dinners at Williams' house.

"Like, we genuinely enjoy our presence on and off the court," Charles said. "Things have been going really fast, and especially when things end, people are gonna have to go to their different (non-WNBA) teams or go home. So we're trying to just intentionally get every moment we can with each other."

Following a scary collapse in Game 3 against Dallas, head coach Natalie Nakase has been sure to make time for herself - primarily to eat and sleep. But this full week off before the Finals meant Nakase got to stick with something she knows and loves.

"Film is my therapy. Basketball is my therapy, so it works hand in hand," she said. "More time gave us more detailed game planning and organization because I feel, yes, we have to play the hardest four quarters of our lives, but we also have to be the smartest."

Nakase did find time between film and sleep to take her coaching staff to a wellness spa nearby.

"We did a sauna, cold plunge, and really bonded in those moments too," she said. "Because we understand valuing our mental and physical health is really important. The way we pour into our players as we coach."

The anticipation is stewing and the long wait finally ends on Saturday afternoon for Game 1. The Finals broadcasts are up against some healthy competition, too.

The San Francisco 49ers face the Washington Commanders on "Monday Night Football" during Game 2 of the Finals, and MLB's World Series coincides with the WNBA's championship round as well. Any potential Game 7 would fall on Halloween for both MLB and the WNBA.

If Friday's fracas is any indication, the Valkyries and Dream series will be can't-miss basketball.

articles.title: Cliff Hagan, Hall of Famer and NBA Champion, dies at 94
articles.summary: Hagan, a 5-time All-Star, helped the St. Louis Hawks break up the Boston Celtics' dynasty with a championship in 1958.
articles.body:
Cliff Hagan, a Hall of Famer who won a 1958 NBA championship with the St. Louis Hawks, has died, the league announced Friday. He was 94.

Hagan, a small forward who earned five consecutive NBA All-Star nods from 1958 to 1962, spent a decade in St. Louis before finishing his career as a player-coach with the ABA's Dallas Chaparrals. Hagan was enshrined in the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame in 1978.

The NBA confirmed the news of Hagan's passing with a statement on social media, describing him as playing "a key role" in the Hawks' championship.

"The NBA is deeply saddened by the passing of Naismith Hall of Famer Cliff Hagan, a five-time All-Star who spent his entire 10-year NBA career with the St. Louis Hawks," the league wrote. "He also won an NCAA championship at Kentucky and later served as a player-coach in the ABA. We extend our heartfelt condolences to Cliff's loved ones and the entire Hawks organization."

Hagan also received a tribute from the Naismith Hall of Fame, where Hagan has been enshrined for nearly 50 years, and from the now-Atlanta Hawks. The Hall of Fame praised Hagan's hook shot and wrote that it was "proud to preserve his legacy."

Prior to going pro, Hagan played at Kentucky, where he was a two-time All-American who helped lead the Wildcats to an NCAA championship in 1951.

One of the peaks of Hagan's career came in that 1958 championship run, as the Hawks broke up the Boston Celtics' dynasty with a 4-2 series win to take the trophy. Though already a key part of the team's shooting, Hagan upped his contributions during the postseason: The forward averaged a double-double throughout the playoffs, with 27.7 points and 10.5 rebounds per game.

The win over Boston also came with a bit of poetic justice, as Hagan had been initially drafted by the Celtics before being immediately traded to St. Louis in exchange for the draft rights to Bill Russell. Two years later, Hagan and the Hawks pulled off the unlikely victory, becoming the only team to beat Boston in the Finals with Russell on the court and legendary head coach Red Auerbach on the sideline.

Bob Pettit, one of Hagan's teammates on that 1958 championship team, also died last month at the age of 93 .

articles.title: LeBron James makes home preseason debut for 76ers with well-rounded performance as Joel Embiid shines
articles.summary: James may be the biggest name on the 76ers. But as Friday's performance showed, he probably isn't the team's star.
articles.body:
LeBron James made his home debut for the Philadelphia 76ers in the team's preseason finale on Friday versus the Boston Celtics. The Sixers lost in overtime, 125-120 .

Introduced second-to-last among the Sixers' starters, before Joel Embiid, James drew the largest ovation from the fans at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season

Embiid won the opening tip-off and the ball went to James. Philadelphia's star free-agent addition then launched a 3-pointer. Had the shot gone in, the crowd would have erupted and given the home team a huge boost. But James missed.

The NBA's all-time leading scorer got his first basket at home in a 76ers uniform nearly midway through the first quarter. James deflected a pass by the Celtics' Hayden Gray to point guard Tyrese Maxey, then streaked down the court with no defenders near him. Maxey floated a lob pass to James, who threw it down for a fast-break dunk.

The two-man game between James and Maxey will likely be a frequent feature of the Sixers' offense, based on what they showed on Friday.

One of James' baskets came after setting a screen at the top of the key, then cutting to the basket and getting a pass from Maxey for a layup. James also brought the ball up the court on several possessions, relieving Maxey of ballhandling responsibilities while also freeing the guard up to move without the ball, going to the basket or moving to the corner for open 3-pointers.

James' night ended with 3:25 remaining in the third quarter with Sixers coach Nick Nurse taking him out for Jaylen Brown. He finished with an all-around performance of 8 points, 8 rebounds and 7 assists in 25 minutes.

Embiid led Philadelphia with 23 points, picking up where he left off versus the Celtics during last season's playoffs . He added 8 rebounds and 5 assists in 29 minutes, noticeably moving across the floor with a frame reportedly 20 to 25 pounds lighter .

Though to be fair, Embiid did not have to face Mitchell Robinson or Neemias Queta, who both sat out Friday's game.

Maxey followed with 22 points and 6 assists, one of three Sixers to score 20 or more points on Friday.

Jaylen Brown faces Celtics after offseason trade

If not for James making his home debut with his new team, Friday's story might have been Brown facing the Celtics for the first time since he was traded to Philadelphia in July.

Brown played 31 minutes, exiting the game at the 7:51 mark of the fourth quarter. He tallied 20 points, 8 rebounds, 3 assists and 2 blocks against his former club.

The Sixers played at Boston last Saturday, but Brown sat out the preseason return to his home court along with fellow starters James, Embiid and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope in a 144-106 defeat .

Notably, Brown did not face former teammate Jayson Tatum as the Celtics sat several starters for Friday's game, including Robinson, former 76er Paul George (part of the trade for Brown) and Derrick White. Both teams opted to play their starters and top contributors in their respective home games during the preseason.

The 76ers begin the 2026-27 regular season on Tuesday at Madison Square Garden against the defending NBA champion New York Knicks. The Celtics will visit the Detroit Pistons, also on Tuesday, to tip off their season.
