articles.title: Dream's Allisha Gray back in full practice, still day-to-day with hand injury ahead of WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Gray is officially 'questionable' for Game 1 of the finals against the Valkyries while recovering from a hand injury sustained in the semifinals.
articles.body:
With the WNBA Finals set to begin on Saturday, star Atlanta Dream guard Allisha Gray is still working her way back from a hand injury. The Dream are returning to the Finals for the first time since 2013, facing the Golden State Valkyries in a highly anticipated matchup.

Gray told reporters on Friday that she is still considered day-to-day with the injury, but said that her pain and recovery has been good. She had her first full practice on Friday, another indicator of an upward trend.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season

"I'll warm up tomorrow and then the medical staff will give me the thumbs up or thumb down. So we'll see," Gray said, via ESPN's Kareem Copeland .

Gray is currently listed as "questionable" to play in Game 1 on the Dream's injury report with a left hand injury.

The Dream lost Gray to the hand injury in Game 1 of the semifinal series against the New York Liberty, with the guard leaving during the first half of the matchup. She then missed the next two games of the three-game sweep .

Earlier this week, Gray told WSBTV's Alison Mastrangelo that she had a minor procedure on her hand, but did not specify what it was. Gray and Atlanta have also kept quiet on the exact nature of the injury, though Gray has been spotted in practice with tape around her left ring and pinky fingers.

In a series that is mostly going to come down to defense , Gray would still be a major presence for the Dream on both ends of the court. Gray led Atlanta in scoring this season, with 19.0 points per game; she finished the regular season seventh in the league in total points. The guard has also averaged 1.4 steals per game, and is a consistent defender on a team that boasts a top-tier defense.

Gray has appeared to be trending toward a return throughout the week, putting up shots with the team on Thursday. Her health, though, will be among the many questions that will define the series. Though Atlanta has proven it can win without Gray on the court, her presence could be a game-changer.

articles.title: Jalen Brunson is afraid to open the bag containing his NBA championship hat because of horrors inside
articles.summary: Jalen Brunson admits his New York Knicks championship hat is still unwashed and sealed in a bag, now reeking of champagne, sweat and cigars.
articles.body: You'd think that a player's NBA Championship hat would be one of their prized possessions, but when it's carrying the potential funk factor that New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson's might be, perhaps not so much. The Knicks locked up their first NBA title in decades back in June, and after all of the festivities, Brunson revealed that his championship lid is still packed away in a bag. And the potential horrors within are keeping him from opening it. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "Mine is still not washed; it’s in the bag, and I’m afraid to open it," Brunson said on a recent episode of his podcast "Roommates Show" with teammate Josh Hart. "It smells terrible: Champagne, sweat, cigars, food, beer, tequila." That sounds like the notes of the worst cologne of all time. That's a recipe for some serious stink, and that's why on the off chance you ever win a championship (hey, it could happen; your church league softball team could be a wagon next season) you've got to suck it up, let it air out and wash it. What you don't want to do is leave it in a sealed bag like Brunson has done. Now he's got a science fair project on his hands. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Not only will that thing smell so bad it'll make your hair fall out, at this point it could have a small civilization growing on it, or it could've sprouted a set of eyes. Three of them. I know someone — it was not me, I swear — who left a sweaty hat in a bag for quite some time, and then, after a bit, put it in their closet. However, this closet was accessed through the bathroom; therefore, it maintained the right level of humidity for some kind of mold or fungus or alien entity to start growing from this hat. It was a horror show, and unfortunately, that may be the fate of Jalen Brunson's NBA Championship hat. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP I hope I'm wrong, but if there's one thing I know, it's the do's and do-not-do's of hat funk.

articles.title: 2026-27 NBA Season Preview: Celtics, Knicks, Raptors, Sixers, Nets (Atlantic Division)
articles.summary: Let's break down what to like and be concerned about, a lineup to watch and a reasonable range for each team to finish in the standings.
articles.body:
With the regular season set to tip off on Oct. 20, let's close out the preview series by taking a look at where each team in the Atlantic Division stands. As always, we'll break down what to like and be concerned about, a lineup to watch and a reasonable range for them to finish in the standings.

Previous divisions: Central • Southwest • Northwest • Pacific • Southeast

It was clear that Jayson Tatum wasn't quite himself as he made his (somewhat surprising) return to action late last season. That version of Tatum averaged 22-10-5 in 16 regular-season games, then ramped that up to 23-11-7 during six playoff games.

It should come as no surprise that, after a full offseason, he looked fantastic in preseason action. The mix of drives, shotmaking, and (improved!) playmaking all popped on film. Do not be surprised by an MVP-level campaign if he stays upright.

I'm pretty excited about Paul George's fit here. For a team that wants to get 3s up, keeps the ball moving with timely passes, and could stand to force more turnovers defensively, George feels pretty hand-in-glove.

Speaking of the defense, I'm ready to watch Derrick White fly around again. Him plus a fun cast of (young) wings, Tatum's versatility (surely the cross-matches will be back), and a pair of quality rim protectors in Neemias Queta and Mitchell Robinson should, once again, lead to an elite unit.

We should know about the bucket-getting by now from Payton Pritchard, but have we seen his comfort as a playmaker during this preseason run? Insert your grains of salt here, but boy does he become even more interesting if he's ready to make a playmaking leap.

Teams really have to deal with 48 minutes of Queta or Robinson on the offensive glass. That doesn't sound like fun at all.

The obvious one is how healthy Tatum and/or George will be. Beyond that, a team that already didn't generate a ton of shots at the rim traded its best guy (Jaylen Brown) for a wing that doesn't really get to the rim anymore in George.

A lot of pressure will be placed on Tatum to "solve" that issue, but I don't know how fair it is to place that heavy of a burden on him with everything else he'll be tasked with. I'm just a little concerned about how jumper-heavy they could be against the league's best, switchiest defenders.

It's obvious to say, but the Celtics really do need healthy campaigns from Tatum and George for all of this to work. I'm curious what kind of maintenance plan we may see from George specifically.

I would expect a bounce-back year in terms of scoring efficiency for White, but it does need to happen. He'll need the shooting to return, lest teams lean further into tossing unders and switches at him. Quietly, he's seen his rim rate drop in each of the past five seasons, with a career-low 7.3% of his shots coming inside of three feet.

LINEUP TO WATCH: Pritchard-George-Tatum-Queta-Robinson

We've already gotten a taste of the double-big look during preseason, but I'm excited to see more of it.

There's plenty of creation available between the Pritchard/George/Tatum triumvirate, with multiple on-and-off ball screening partners to play with. This is also the most size you could put around Pritchard defensively, if you're worried about that sort of thing.

The Celtics already have the (regular season) formula down: suppress turnovers, win the glass, take a ton of 3s, and keep their opponents off the free-throw line. Staying true to those principles, paired with (or at least, headlined by) an MVP-caliber season from Tatum, feels like an easy-to-envision pathway to the East's top seed.

The East is tough, which could put them in the 7-10 range by default. Beyond that, there's a level of production needed from the big-name wings (Tatum, George) for this team to reach its ceiling. Injury woes to either would limit the floor, and I do have mild concerns about how jumper-dependent the team may be.

Any time you can win a championship and bring back virtually everyone of consequence, you have to do it.

There's obvious star power here. You have two-way versatility. The bench unit may not contain an A+ reserve, but it's filled with complementary, scalable talent. Mike Brown is a fantastic coach with a stronger proof-of-concept to point to now. The vibes should be high here.

Sign me up for even more Karl-Anthony Towns (pay him!) usage as a hub. His ability to stretch out defenses with his shooting, make decisions as a passer, and attack different types of defenders off the bounce makes him one of the most unique talents in the league. He should be phenomenal in Year 2 of this system.

Jalen Brunson is one of the most ridiculous (complimentary) bucket-getters I've ever seen, especially at his size. I'm excited to watch him continue frying defenders.

Having a wing/forward trio of OG Anunoby (hopefully he finally makes an All-Star team), Mikal Bridges (LIMBS!), and Josh Hart (pay him, too!) is such a luxury, man. It's a pleasure to watch them guard and toggle matchups with ease.

Hey uh … have we seen Andre Drummond this preseason? They may not miss Mitchell Robinson all that much if this is the version they're going to get.

They just won a championship and most of the rotation remains intact. I don't have major questions here.

The most pressing thing for me is what level of force and focus they come out of the gates with. They have a proven, title-winning formula they can lean on; will they be locked in enough, particularly on the defensive end, to get through the slog of the regular season with top-tier seeding, or will they prioritize getting through healthy and hopefully ramping things up by the end of the year?

I generally believe in the second unit, but there's a stray "what if the guard creation goes backwards?" thought at the back of my head.

As good as Drummond has looked in limited preseason play, he simply isn't the down-to-down rim protector that Robinson was or is. I do wonder, in light of some of the Towns questions and some of the back-of-roster injuries (and waiving) if that'll be an issue that perks up this year.

More of a complaint than a concern: I can't believe Towns and Hart didn't get paid before the season. I expect both to be professional but come on.

LINEUP TO WATCH: Brunson-Shamet-Bridges-Anunoby-Towns

Since Shamet joined the Knicks back in 2024-25, he's logged 161 minutes with the starters in place of Hart. The Knicks have won those minutes by 55 points (+9.0 net rating) while shooting "only" 35.5% from 3 as a unit.

Shamet in the lineup for Hart largely takes the big-on-wing gambit off the table for defenses, unless they want to risk it with Anunoby. I'd like to see more of this look.

The defending champs, fresh off one of the most dominant playoff runs in NBA history, are returning nine of their top-10 players in playoff minutes per game. Continuity, good health, and a heightened level of consistency on the defensive end would put the top seed in play.

Regular season boredom could be enough for them to slide down the standings in a tougher Eastern Conference. Within that lens, I'd keep an eye on how consistently they hit the right notes defensively.

WHAT TO LIKE: Scottie Barnes, leveling up

Barnes has been one of the league's most versatile players almost from the time he stepped foot in the league. The defense is DPOY-level, and he's able to oscillate between on-ball and dirty-work duties offensively.

Watching him turn the scoring aggression up to 11 during last year's postseason moved me. Seeing him sustain that aggression during preseason action has me ready to make some incredibly bold predictions concerning him. For now, though, I'll just say I'm excited to watch him play basketball.

Adding Kawhi Leonard to this group is an instant ceiling-raiser. He's coming off the best scoring season of his career, and should both fit naturally in a lot of the off-ball actions that head coach Darko Rajaković has baked into Toronto's half-court offense, and serve as a clear-a-side security blanket whenever they need him. Oh, the roster context allows him to continue being utilized in a primary off-ball role defensively. Good luck passing or dribbling around him.

Collin Murray-Boyles as a concept. Yes. Please and thank you. I'll be keeping an eye on the non-rim scoring — touch shots, middies, the occasional 3 — but I'm a big fan of pretty much everything else.

I'm ready for Jamal Shead and Ja'Kobe Walter to be incredibly rude to opposing reserves. I'm excited for the Raptors defense in general.

BIGGEST QUESTION MARK: Half-court offense

Kawhi was brought in to (help) solve the issue, but it's worth monitoring what things will look like when he's on the bench. My baseline worry is less about the talent — though I do have overall shooting questions for the roster — and more about how teams will guard them.

Will Barnes' aggression, if it continues, make him a more consistent draw-two threat? Can Immanuel Quickley or RJ Barrett score (efficiently) enough to garner more aggressive coverages? If defenses are largely OK with switching and staying home, I'd be less enthused about their prospects.

Though Murray-Boyles is the future of the frontcourt, the Raptors do still need the screening and general connective work that Jakob Poeltl provides. Ideally, he'd serve as a competent bridge to the more fruitful Barnes-Murray-Boyles minutes. I just hope Poeltl is healthy enough to provide that service.

More curiosity than concern, but I wonder where the Raptors land in terms of their pick-up points defensively. They started incredibly high last year before getting torched — and ultimately dialing back the pressure a bit.

LINEUP TO WATCH: Quickley-Barrett-Leonard-Barnes-Murray-Boyles

Let the record reflect that the only reason I didn't continue the top-seed trend here is because I don't believe Kawhi will play enough regular-season games to take some of my half-court and offense and shooting questions off the table. He may simply be the answer in a playoff context.

Their elite defense and transition attack is still enough of a formula to churn out wins, especially if Barnes takes another step forward.

If this is a 40-game (or worse) campaign from Kawhi, familiar questions on the offensive end could lower their ceiling. Those, plus the overall strength of the conference, could have them in the 7-10 range.

Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, LeBron James, and Joel Embiid in the same lineup sounds like some 2K nonsense. That it's a real thing — with Brown and James being acquired within three weeks of each other — is kinda wild!

Man, that's so much talent to play with, though. Maxey and Brown are downhill demons in their own right who should juice Philly's transition attack. LeBron and Embiid are half-court pillars that can force defenses into tough decisions. I'm excited to see how quickly these four are able to build chemistry with each other.

VJ Edgecombe has "two-way star" written all over him, especially as he grows as a half-court scorer. Being able to play off the gravity of four All-Star caliber players should make for an easy context, even if I'd selfishly love for him to get a healthy dose of self-creation reps to accelerate his growth.

I've been saying it pretty consistently this summer, but I'm such a big fan of the Dean Wade fit. A big wing defender willing to fill gaps on the other end — cut, hit the offensive glass, and make connective passes — should vibe nicely with this group.

Actually, to zoom out: I really appreciate the work Philly did with this bench. Snagging Wade, Anfernee Simons, and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope (if he's rejuvenated in a win-now spot) could turn out to be really stealthy work.

BIGGEST QUESTION MARK: Frontcourt health

I don't have to spill much virtual ink on the importance of LeBron and Embiid staying healthy. The Sixers simply won't reach their ceiling without them. A quieter subplot worth monitoring is the depth behind Embiid.

Adem Bona isn't back yet ( though he should be soon ), and Ariel Hukporti is unfortunately out for the season after rupturing his Achilles. A world where Embiid and his backup plans are hurt, especially with the Sixers' financial limitations, does not sound like a fun one.

I'll just say I'm fascinated to see what level they can get this defense to. There's a chance they're more than solid, with Brown giving more consistent effort with a lighter scoring load, Edgecombe continuing to grow on that end, Maxey's continued buy-in, and the back-line roaming (and communication) of LeBron and Embiid. It could also go the other way, with the off-ball defense in particular giving me headaches. We shall see!

Tied to that, the Sixers were one of the worst defensive rebounding teams in the league last year ( 69.1 defensive rebound rate, 27th ). They weren't much better with Embiid on the floor . I have some real questions about how consistently they'll be able to end possessions.

LINEUP TO WATCH: Maxey-Simons-Edgecombe-Wade-Bona

The starters are the easy call, but I'm fascinated by what the staggering is going to look like. There hasn't been much to glean from on the preseason front, but I'd like to see them keep Maxey and Edgecombe paired together. Let the young guys push the pace, while LeBron and Embiid could lead a more methodical attack. If it does play out that way, I'd be interested in seeing this group together.

The pathway is simple: the Core Four meshes well (and plays 60+ games together), Edgecombe continues to progress, and an underrated bench unit fills gaps at a high level. The potential is certainly there.

There are obvious health concerns with Embiid, and age concerns with LeBron. The depth behind Embiid is worthy of questions, even if I'm personally enamored with some of their options. There's a world where health concerns limit the ceiling, and defensive concerns (especially the rebounding) limit their floor.

Last year, I was in on the Nets having a sneaky good defense; they gave me only one good month , but boy was I vindicated for that singular month!

My intrigue is on the other end this time around. Michael Porter Jr. is coming off a career-high campaign where his shooting led the dance, but his passing chops popped in a way we weren't accustomed to seeing. Add in a chip-on-shoulder Julius Randle to put pressure on the rim, be moved around the board, and introduce his own brand of playmaking, and the Nets quietly have two pillars to make life easier on everyone else.

Egor Dëmin shot the leather off the ball as a rookie, a pleasant surprise based on some of the pre-draft intel that surrounded him. Sadly, he didn't get to the rim enough to complement that shooting, or unlock avenues for his passing chops to shine. Summer league plus preseason play has been a whole lot of Dëmin putting his head down and generating deeper paint touches. Consider me amused.

With that, I've liked a lot of what I've seen from Mikel Brown Jr. so far. He has some real juice as a creator, and a poise in ball screens that should serve him well moving forward. Him plus Dëmin could be a fascinating duo for years to come.

Noah Clowney and Day'Ron Sharpe aren't household names, but they're quality basketball players that I'm excited to see more of. Clowney shoots, is comfortable creating off the bounce, and flies around defensively (though that's not always a good thing). Sharpe entered the league as an offensive rebounding monster, and has since shown more comfort as a passing hub, shooter, and at-the-level defender.

I was bullish on the Nets' defense last year because of the cast of wings they had — and the full-court pressure they could provide — along with the versatility of Nic Claxton when healthy. A lot of those wings are gone (though Keon Ellis and Terance Mann certainly aren't slouches), Claxton is in Chicago, and there will be a lot of Porter Jr. and Randle minutes.

I will not be making any bold proclamations about this unit, though head coach Jordi Fernandez will earn Coach of the Year equity from me if he's able to establish a level of competence.

While I'm generally intrigued by the offense, a team with this many young guards in the rotation just screams "we will struggle with turnovers at some point." They're going to hum on their best nights, but I worry a little about their per-possession consistency.

How long are Randle and/or Porter Jr. going to be here, exactly? And if they're moved, what will that do for the development context of Brown Jr. and Dëmin?

LINEUP TO WATCH: Brown Jr.-Dëmin-Porter Jr.-Clowney-Sharpe

This is the "let 'em hoop" group for me. Give Brown Jr. and Dëmin a runway offensively; let Clowney and Sharpe be chaos agents defensively. Porter Jr. is there to get shots up when called upon, or at least open up space for everyone else. This is quietly a pretty big lineup, too. They'll likely lose their minutes together, but I at least want to see it.

There are two All-Star-caliber players on the roster; a chip-on-the-shoulder campaign from Randle and another flame-throwing season from Porter Jr. could give the Nets a higher baseline than given credit for. Dëmin growth, Brown Jr. looking comfortable early, some interesting frontcourt pieces (Sharpe, Clowney) with Jordi Fernandez pulling the strings … I'd keep an eye out.

This could be a turnover-heavy offense paired with an awful defense. I would imagine the top-end talent (Randle, Porter Jr.) will be in trade rumors; the Nets cashing in on either of them would make the team worse in the short term. Worst record in the East is in play.

articles.title: NBA trade update: 6-foot-5 guard returns to LA Clippers on a two-way contract in a surprising roster move
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Clippers have brought Cam Christie back on a two-way contract, just days after waiving him.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Clippers have brought Cam Christie back on a two-way contract, just days after waiving him. ESPN’s Shams Charania reported the agreement on Friday. The 21-year-old guard cleared waivers and is back with the club that drafted the Minnesota product in 2024. It is a quick reversal for a player who appeared in 55 games last season and enters a third year in Los Angeles. Defense is what Christie is known for, and the Clippers clearly still value it. The new deal arrives with opening week around the corner.Why did the Clippers bring back Cam Christie on a two-way deal?Clearing waivers made the reunion possible. No other team claimed the 6-foot-5 guard, so Los Angeles was free to sign Christie again on new terms. Charania reported both moves, the waiver early in the week and the new contract on Friday.Coach Ty Lue singled out Christie’s “elite defense” last season, and the two-way contract keeps that skill in the organization. Los Angeles took Christie 46th overall in 2024, the 16th selection of the second round. The debut came on Dec. 4 of that year, and the career total is 68 NBA games.Christie’s brother, Max, also plays in the NBA.At 6-foot-5 and 190 pounds, Christie shoots right-handed and was born July 24, 2005, in Arlington Heights, Illinois. Rolling Meadows High School and Minnesota came before the draft.What role can Christie fill for the Clippers this season?Christie played 55 games last season and never started one, averaging 8.7 minutes, 2.8 points, 1.4 rebounds and 0.6 assists. Shooting was a struggle, with 38.1 percent from the field and 24.5 percent from three, where the guard went 12 for 49. Free throws were the steadier number at 76 percent.The rookie year was smaller still. Christie logged 13 games and 4.5 minutes a night in 2024-25, and one game against Portland last season brought a single minute.Career highs sit at 17 points and nine rebounds. Stretch the work to 36 minutes and the line looks better: 11.7 points, 5.9 rebounds and 2.3 assists. A statistical projection for 2026-27 goes higher on scoring, at 13.4 points per 36 minutes.The defensive reputation has not shown up in last season’s advanced numbers. Defensive box plus-minus came in at minus-1.1 over 480 minutes, though it is a small sample.Minor injuries added to the picture. Right foot soreness kept Christie out of one game against Oklahoma City, and ankle and abdominal issues put the guard on the questionable list before games against Detroit and Chicago. articles.title: Caleb Wilson's Final Box Score Stats, Highlights from Wolves vs. Bulls Preseason
articles.summary: Chicago Bulls rookie forward Caleb Wilson played his final preseason game on Friday before his regular season debut, and he fared well in a 133-116 home victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves.
articles.body:
Chicago Bulls rookie forward Caleb Wilson played his final preseason game on Friday before his regular season debut, and he fared well in a 133-116 home victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Over five preseason games, Wilson averaged 15.8 points on 44.1 percent shooting, 4.4 rebounds and 2.8 assists in 26.6 minutes per game.

The former UNC star's explosiveness was evident early.

He also got it done on the defensive end, blocking shots with both hands:

Wilson's energy and athleticism are going to cause problems for teams, as they did on this putback late in the first quarter:

Chicago is beginning a rebuild under new leadership, as Executive Vice President of Basketball Operations Bryson Graham and head coach Tiago Splitter are now running the show.

Wilson, the No. 4 overall pick in the NBA draft, is a centerpiece of the Bulls' present and future and should be heavily featured this year. Fans will see him on Wednesday, when Chicago begins the season at the Toronto Raptors.

articles.title: Joel Embiid Drops Hilarious Quote After Viral Video of Huge Dunk in 76ers Preseason Game
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star Joel Embiid surprised himself by dunking in Friday preseason action again the Boston Celtics.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star Joel Embiid surprised himself by dunking in Friday preseason action again the Boston Celtics.

"I guess it's good to dunk. I thought I would never dunk again. I guess, I don't know what happened. I kind of got possessed," Embiid told reporters Friday (h/t Sixers Wire's Ky Carlin).

Embiid, who has missed significant stretches of his career due to knee injuries, joked two weeks ago he had made "probably the last dunk of my career" in a Sixers team scrimmage.

The 76ers wrapped up their exhibition slate with Friday night's overtime loss to the Celtics. Embiid will now prepare to open his 11th regular season with the Sixers in a Tuesday away game against the defending champion New York Knicks.

articles.title: Michael Beasley Beats Delonte West by 1st-Round KO in Boxing Fight of Former NBA Players
articles.summary: Former NBA players Michael Beasley and Delonte West fought on the Brandrisk 16 boxing card in Miami on Friday evening. Beasley won via first-round TKO.
articles.body:
Former NBA players Michael Beasley and Delonte West fought on the Brandrisk 16 boxing card in Miami on Friday evening. Beasley won via first-round TKO.

Beasley played 11 NBA seasons (2008-2019) for seven teams, including the Miami Heat, who selected the former Kansas State star with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2008 draft. The forward averaged 12.4 points and 4.7 rebounds per game.

West played eight NBA campaigns (2004-2012) for four teams. He starred for a 2003-04 St. Joseph's team that won all 27 of its regular season games and got drafted 24th overall by the Boston Celtics in 2004. He posted 9.7 points and 3.6 assists per game.

articles.title: LeBron James Responds to Helicopter Question amid Criticism Before Start of 76ers Season
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James doesn't think it's out of the ordinary to be commuting from New York in a helicopter ahead of his first season with the Sixers.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James doesn't think it's out of the ordinary to be commuting from New York in a helicopter ahead of his first season with the Sixers.

"I've done it before," James said Friday when asked if he had ever traveled to work in the aircraft (h/t ESPN's Kris Rhim).

James concluded, "Just another way of transportation, that's all."

ESPN's Dave McMenamin initially reported James would be splitting his time between Philadelphia and New York this season while using a helicopter to cut a potential two-hour commute to around 40 minutes .

According to Front Office Sports' Daniel Roberts and TMZ Sports , James has been granted use of a Fanatics aviation, including a helicopter, as part of an endorsement deal with the company.

After closing out the preseason Friday night in Philadelphia, James will be back in New York by next week. The Sixers are scheduled to open the regular season Tuesday with a road game against the New York Knicks.

articles.title: Darryn Peterson, Ace Bailey's Final Box Score Stats, Highlights from Jazz vs. Suns Preseason
articles.summary: The Utah Jazz played their final 2026 preseason game on Friday evening and beat the host Phoenix Suns, 119-116.
articles.body:
The Utah Jazz played their final 2026 preseason game on Friday evening and beat the host Phoenix Suns, 119-116.

Utah's top picks in each of the last two drafts—Darryn Peterson (No. 2 overall in 2026) and Ace Bailey (No. 5 in 2025)—took part in this matchup. Here's how they performed.

Peterson's has impressed at times this preseason, perhaps nevermore than when he scored 23 points on 10-of-18 shooting against the Denver Nuggets on Oct. 6.

On Friday, Peterson didn't have the best shooting night, but he had four points and an assist in the last 2:16 to help put this game away.

Twelve points on just three field goal attempts is awfully impressive, and that's what Bailey did Friday in his best preseason showing. He'll be a big asset off the bench in Utah this season.

As for the highlights, Peterson got Utah going with a quick baseline jumper just outside the line after a nice crossover.

Peterson soon found Bailey for an alley-oop dunk in transition:

The Suns tried to pull away in the third, when they went up by as many as 13 points. Peterson made some big plays to help prevent Phoenix from making it worse, though.

Utah ultimately went on a 28-9 run over a nearly 10-minute span in the third and fourth quarters and took a 104-98 lead with six minutes left in the final frame. The Jazz then took a late edge on the aforementioned Peterson bucket and kept Denver at arm's length from there.

The Jazz will begin the regular season on Wednesday at the Memphis Grizzlies.

articles.title: Warriors reportedly waiving ex-76ers 6-foot-6 wing, former first-round pick after preseason
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors have made a decision on their roster. They will be waiving one of their wings that was released by the Philadelphia 76ers this summ...
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors spent much of the summer trying to piece together their roster after missing out on LeBron James and Anthony Davis. They ultimately assembled a roster with enough depth to help support Steph Curry and Draymond Green.

One of the additions was former first-round pick Dalen Terry, whom Golden State signed to a non-guaranteed deal.

"The Golden State Warriors and Dalen Terry have agreed to a deal, league sources told hoopshype. Terry, the 18th pick of the 2022 NBA Draft, has played four combined NBA seasons with the Chicago Bulls and Philadelphia 76ers ," HoopsHype's Michael Scotto wrote.

Terry was originally drafted by the Chicago Bulls before joining the Philadelphia 76ers in February of last season. Philadelphia looked to develop him, but the organization eventually needed to clear roster space for LeBron James and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope.

"The Sixers waive Dalen Terry to clear space for LeBron James and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope. Terry, a former first-round pick, had a non-guaranteed contract for the upcoming season. Philadelphia must still move one additional player to create enough room for both additions," NBA writer Jake Weinbach wrote.

With the regular season approaching, the Warriors need to finalize their 15-man roster. Terry will be one of the players affected by those roster decisions.

"The Warriors are planning on waiving Dalen Terry before Monday and having him join the Santa Cruz Warriors, sources told ClutchPoints. Terry is a player the Warriors like and will continue developing in the G League. Tonight is the team's final preseason game against POR," NBA insider Brett Siegel posted.

The positive for Terry is that Golden State still sees potential in him and wants to continue developing him. The Warriors are giving him an opportunity to improve in the G League, but he will need to make the most of that chance if he hopes to return to the NBA.

This does not have to be the end of Terry's NBA aspirations. He can continue working on his game with the Santa Cruz Warriors and try to earn another opportunity at the highest level. For now, however, his path back to the NBA will likely begin in the G League.

articles.title: 1 Cavs player in danger of losing starting job in 2026-27 training camp
articles.summary: The Cleveland Cavaliers, at the very least, got over the Conference Finals hump during their postseason run in 2026. The problem, of course, was that the eve...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Cavaliers , at the very least, got over the Conference Finals hump during their postseason run in 2026. The problem, of course, was that the eventual NBA champion New York Knicks swept them . There remains plenty of urgency for the Cavs to find a breakthrough, especially after they traded away Darius Garland for James Harden, and their moves this offseason show that the front office is all-in on this core of theirs.

Throughout the Donovan Mitchell era, the three-spot has been a bit of a hole for the Cavs. They have tried to deploy Isaac Okoro, Max Strus, and De'Andre Hunter to fill that void, but none of them have stuck. Of those players, Strus did the best job as a rugged defender and movement shooter, but Cleveland knew that this was a position they needed to upgrade in.

Considering that the Cavs were in second apron hell not too long ago, it's quite remarkable of them to pull off a sign-and-trade for up-and-coming combo forward Peyton Watson — giving them a long-term solution at a position of need.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

With that said, it doesn't appear as though any Cavs player is in danger of losing a starting spot heading into the 2026-27 campaign.

Peyton Watson is the nailed-on starter for the Cavs at the three

18 different players started at least one game for the Cavs last season. Even Evan Mobley came off the bench on two occasions. But this is a team that has prioritized continuity, and as long as they're healthy, there will not be much movement in the starting lineup.

There's no reason to expect head coach Kenny Atkinson to make many changes, if any at all, to his starting lineup. Their All-Star backcourt of Mitchell and Harden remains, and their frontcourt is set with Mobley and Jarrett Allen running it back for the sixth consecutive season.

Prior to the signing of Watson, it would have been interesting to see who the Cavs would have started in an alternative universe where the Denver Nuggets bit the second apron bullet. Perhaps Cleveland would have started Strus regularly yet again, or maybe new signing Mario Hezonja , after impressing in the EuroLeague, could make his case for a spot in the starting five.

But the Cavs did not trade away a 2031 first-round pick, one of their few tradeable draft assets, and sign Watson to a four-year, $88 million contract to have him come off the bench.

Watson was making plenty of strides on offense in the middle of the 2025-26 season; amid the Nuggets' injury woes, there was a stretch from December 22 until February 4 where Watson nailed a starting role and was incredible on a nightly basis.

During that aforementioned stretch, Watson averaged 19.5 points, 5.0 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 1.2 steals, and 1.3 blocks on 49/43/73 shooting splits. Nikola Jokic did miss 16 of the Nuggets' 25 games during that stretch, which, without a doubt, helped inflate Watson's stats.

But it's a testament to his improved skill level that he was able to put up those stats while receiving more defensive attention and less help from his three-time MVP teammate.

The Cavs won't have the usage opening for Watson to fill the stat sheet the way he did during that eye-opening stretch. But that doesn't mean that they aren't all-in on him as a member of this core.

Not only can he wreak havoc defensively, he was much-improved from beyond the arc as well (41.1% last season), making him a valuable off-ball weapon for Harden and Mitchell to feed. Moreover, Watson's improved game off the bounce means that defenses simply cannot ignore him or close out on him hard.

This makes it so that none of the Cavs' starters are actually under much of a threat to lose their spot. What's more interesting to monitor is how the Cavs will divvy up the minutes off the bench.

Who will be the fixtures off the bench for Kenny Atkinson?

Without a doubt, Jaylon Tyson and Sam Merrill will be featuring prominently in the Cavs' rotation. Merrill can pick up opposing guards for 94 feet, while Tyson impressed as a glue-guy last season , averaging 13.2 points per game while making two triples per game on a 44.6% clip.

Hezonja should also be one of the first guys off the bench for Atkinson. Last season, in 66 games across EuroLeague and Liga ACB, Hezonja averaged nearly 15 points per contest on 44/33/87 shooting splits. He can be a huge weapon in transition, and he also provides some defensive tenacity on the wing.

Nae'Qwan Tomlin, the team's resident dirty work guy, Thomas Bryant, the veteran backup big, and Craig Porter Jr. should also get some minutes here and there. Tyrese Proctor and Meleek Thomas may not be in the rotation every night, but they should get some chances to impress and earn minutes.

articles.title: El invicto Estu reclama actitud y afición ante su primer gran reto de la temporada
articles.standfirst: Recibe al Iberolea Palencia en el Movistar Arena
articles.summary: Recibe al Iberolea Palencia en el Movistar Arena
articles.body: La Primera FEB se prepara para su primera final. Y eso que sólo estamos en la cuarta jornada. Una fecha que aparece ya como una de esas que están marcadas en rojo al comienzo de cada curso. Y más por cómo han empezado los dos protagonistas del duelo con más interés de esta semana en un campeonato en el que cualquier mínimo fallo se paga con creces. Precisamente eso es lo que quiere evitar un Movistar Estudiantes que marcha lider invicto en la tabla y que recibe en su casa, el Movistar Arena, a un Iberolea Palencia que le pisa los talones en la clasificación con el mismo número de victorias en el casillero: tres en tres partidos. Todo un partidazo que llevará implícito algo más que una victoria ya que su poseedor podrá seguir una semana más sin conocer la derrota y tras haberse impuesto a un rival directo en la lucha por el ascenso. Consciente de la importancia del choque (y de llevarse el triunfo) los jugadores de Movistar Estudiantes han hecho un llamamiento a filas a todos los suyos. En boca de Jehyve Floyd el club colegial ha pedido a la afición que acuda en masa al Movistar Arena (aún quedan entradas a la venta) para afrontar el primer gran partido del curso y, de paso, tomarse su particular revancha ante el equipo de Natxo Lezcano, que la pasada temporada les ganó en los dos envites que disputaron. “Es un partido durísimo. Dos equipos que estamos defendiendo bien, dos equipos que son solo tres jornadas pero estamos recibiendo pocos puntos. Queremos también rebotear los dos y que el rebote sea parte de nuestro dominio de los partidos y así está siendo en los dos casos”, aseguraba Toni Ten en la previa del duelo. “Un partido en donde va a ser duro, un partido donde el rebote va a ser muy importante y un partido en el que los dos equipos tenemos talento en ataque. Vamos a ver quién es el que es capaz de dominar el ritmo del partido y vamos a ver qué jugadores de talento son capaces de hacerlo mejor”. Por su parte, el preparador del conjunto palentino destacó la importancia del choque en un “escenario especial. Para ganar a Estudiantes necesitamos que todo el mundo esté a su máximo nivel y necesitamos provocar que tengan un mal día, porque si tienen un muy buen día te van a ganar. Es un equipo top de la categoría y que cuenta con una muy buena plantilla”. No es un fin de semana más para el conjunto del Estudiantes. Si el primer equipo masculino se juega el liderato, el primer equipo femenino se juega volver a retomar la senda de la victoria ante un equipo ante el que todavía no vencer en su pista. Las Women in Black viajan hasta el Palau d’Esports de la Seu d’Urgell para intentar conseguir romper la racha ante su bestia negra a domicilio. Por su parte, el equipo de Segunda FEB también tendrá su particular reto: conseguir conjugar el verbo vencer por primera vez esta temporada. El conjunto colegual recibe al CB Starlabs Morón, un equipo “con carácter”, según el técnico colegial Mariano Arasa. “Es un conjunto bastante estructurado que tiene las cosas claras y que tiene puntos en el perímetro con buenos generadores”. Argumentos que presentan un rival complicado y ante los que los colegiales quieren hacer valer el factor cancha como elemento diferencial.

articles.title: Biggest Winners and Losers from 2026 NBA Preseason
articles.summary: The NBA doesn't crown a champion or hand out awards for preseason play, but dismissing exhibition games as meaningless is a mistake.
articles.body:
The NBA doesn't crown a champion or hand out awards for preseason play, but dismissing exhibition games as meaningless is a mistake.

The preseason offers the first hints about which rookies are ready to report for duty, which teams might already be behind the injury eight ball and which theoretical contenders might be even more formidable in practice.

This year, the Memphis Grizzlies used the preseason to showcase their exciting new core, while the retooled Philadelphia 76ers got a terrifying glimpse into their potential frailties. Nothing we've seen so far is set in stone, but a few clear signs are worth reading into.

Let's get our bearings before opening night by checking in on the 2026 NBA preseason winners and losers.

Zach Edey is meeting athletic forwards at the rim , Cam Boozer already looks like a legitimate offensive hub, and GG Jackson seems primed for a leap.

In other words, there's been a whole lot to like about the Memphis Grizzlies this preseason.

Boozer is probably the most important of Memphis' frontcourt trio, and he's been as good as advertised. The rookie forward appears slimmer and more athletic than he did at Duke, but his leaner look isn't limiting his power. He had several forceful drives and finishes against the Bulls on Oct. 9 and has had no issue bullying his way to the foul line.

The quick processing and unselfishness that defined Boozer's game in college are intact, only now they're buttressed by improved self-sufficient scoring.

The Grizzlies ended an era by shipping out Desmond Bane, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Ja Morant over roughly 13 months. The preseason suggests they've already laid the foundation for a new one.

It's an annual tradition to fixate on how many games Joel Embiid will be able to play in the upcoming season. Recent history says that number could be anywhere between zero and 50, and that uncertainty is the one great variable in the Philadelphia 76ers' outlook.

Based on his preseason debut, Embiid's number of games might matter less than the quality. Or lack thereof.

In his debut against the Brooklyn Nets on Oct. 8, Embiid shot just 1-of-5 from the field, turned the ball over eight times and moved like he was stuck in mud. This, by the way, might be as physically spry as the former MVP is going to look at any point during the year.

You don't get to fret about Embiid's ability to hold up physically over several months and also act as if he's going to work his way into shape. Not even after an improved showing in the team's final preseason contest.

Odds are Embiid will still be able to threaten defenses as a spot-up weapon, and he's not going to throw the ball all over the gym once he's used to his new teammates. But his preseason debut raised fresh concerns about how much athleticism he can recover after so many injuries.

The Oklahoma City Thunder are one of the only teams that could afford to lose three rotation players in a cost-cutting summer, and that was before it seemed clear that rookie Bennett Stirtz was ready to take on a significant role.

The Iowa product racked up 61 points and drilled 13 threes across his first three preseason games, handing out 13 assists for good measure. While most assumed Cason Wallace would pick up the bulk of the minutes made available by the departures of Lu Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe, it appears Stirtz is worthy of some, too.

Perhaps most importantly, Stirtz's offensive production could address what might be the Thunder's only real needs. OKC won the 2025 championship in spite of occasionally substandard half-court creation and spacing, two areas in which Stirtz excelled during the exhibition season.

In a draft class that saw plenty of point guards come off the board in the top 10, OKC's No. 16 pick is so far outproducing all of them.

If you believed the Charlotte Hornets were going to prove their doubters wrong by winning at least as many games without LaMelo Ball this season as they did with him last year, well...you probably assumed the revamped roster was going to stay healthy.

The preseason hasn't exactly been a good omen on that front.

Kon Knueppel suffered a hamstring strain during an offseason workout that has kept him out of action. Coby White, whose assumption of primary playmaking duties was always going to be critical in a post-Ball world, strained his calf.

Then Brandon Miller, no stranger to injuries during his three-year career, missed the preseason opener with a shin contusion before returning to score 18 points against Milwaukee.

There's still a ton to like about the Hornets. They pulled off a heist in trading Miles Bridges to the Suns, figure to score in bunches using a triple-heavy style and still have a shot to be a better collective unit without Ball. But all of those positives shrink in importance if several key players can't be in top form by the time the real games start.

It's going to take some time for the Milwaukee Bucks to rebuild after trading Giannis Antetokounmpo, but their preseason play has offered nothing but hope about the tools they've assembled for the task.

Kel'el Ware turned in a pair of double-doubles in his first two appearances, even starting alongside Myles Turner in a rare "double-big, double-stretch" frontcourt combo. The third-year big man is a potentially dominant threat above the rim and shoots the deep ball with smooth, confident form.

Tyler Herro, another piece that came back in the Antetokounmpo deal, may not be a potential keeper like Ware. But he'll be a valuable trade chip if he continues his preseason trend of logging more points than shot attempts.

Rookie Brayden Burries was Milwaukee's Summer League story, while fellow newcomers Jaime Jaquez Jr. and Kasparas Jakucionis have also shown positive preseason flashes.

The Bucks may not intend to win a ton of games during the upcoming regular season, but their road back to respectability looks promising.

Stats courtesy of NBA.com , Basketball Reference and Cleaning the Glass . Salary info via Spotrac .

Grant Hughes covers the NBA for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, where he appears with Bleacher Report's Dan Favale .

articles.title: What Exactly Is Bronny James' Role On the Los Angeles Lakers?
articles.summary: Bronny James' $2.3 million salary for 2026-27 is guaranteed. That's the good news. The rest? It's pretty cloudy after the young guard's third NBA preseason.
articles.body:
Bronny James' $2.3 million salary for 2026-27 is guaranteed. That's the good news. The rest? It's pretty cloudy after the young guard's third NBA preseason.

Friday, in the Los Angeles Lakers' finale to the exhibition slate, Bronny didn't take the floor till just before the start of the fourth quarter. He played that entire last frame. And he finished with no points on 0-of-1 shooting, turned it over once and handed out one assist in 12 minutes.

For the preseason, he had not-exactly-eye-popping averages of 16.4 minutes, 2.2 points, 2.8 assists and 2.6 turnovers. Even more alarming, when you stretch that last number out to a per-36-minute average, it's 5.7. Yes, 5.7 turnovers per 36 minutes.

Since he left USC after averaging 4.8 points and shooting 36.6 percent from the field as a freshman, Bronny has had his moments as a pro, mostly in the G-League.

In those positive moments, his bounce is often on display. Even relative to other pros, he's a solid (though unspectacular) athlete. He typically works hard on the defensive end. And in true "son of an NBA star" fashion, he has a lot of the fundamentals down.

Friday, he had a boxout against the Denver Nuggets that drove his opponent all the way into the stanchion. The Lakers snagged that rebound, but they lost the game, 121-106. And by the final buzzer, that solitary boxout was probably Bronny's best play of the night.

Earlier in (and really throughout) the preseason, his most memorable moments may have been his inability to bring the ball up the floor against even mild pressure.

That's a problem for a guard. It's a bigger one for a guard listed at 6'2". And as he enters his third NBA season, there's really no excuse for it.

By now, whether his coaches or front office have told him or not (surely, they have), Bronny should know that his NBA survival is heavily dependent on his ability to handle the basketball. Whatever amount of time he's poured into it, it doesn't appear to have been enough.

James' shooting really hasn't come along to any acceptable degree either. He finished this preseason 4-of-16 from the field and 1-of-8 (12.5 percent) from deep. In 106 summer league, preseason, regular season and postseason appearances, Bronny is now shooting 35.7 percent from the field and 26.8 percent from three.

Not far off those uninspiring shooting numbers from his lone season with the Trojans.

So, assuming L.A. doesn't eat that guaranteed money and waive James (they likely won't), what exactly can he do for the Lakers this season?

At the risk of sounding condescending, he has to be a good end-of-the-bench teammate, and that doesn't necessarily just mean enthusiastic celebrations.

It may not be enough to get and keep him on the floor right now, but the aforementioned athleticism and fundamentals make Bronny a passable defender. If he can now add a little more intensity to that mix, James can bring some real value outside of games.

He's capable of pushing the regulars in practice, to a degree that actually helps them get better. And the longer and more consistently he provides value in that way, the more likely JJ Redick is to give him a shot to do it in games.

To answer the question in the headline more directly: Bronny's specific role is almost certainly the one he's had the last couple seasons. He is, at best, a third-stringer. He hasn't proved worthy of more.

But even third-stringers can make statements when they're on the floor, particularly on the hustle and defense fronts.

In all likelihood, we've spent too much mental energy waiting for James to show up elsewhere—whether as a shooter, passer or ball-handler—when his actual calling card may simply have to be energy.

articles.title: ‘All in, all the time': How the Valkyries redefined what's elite in the WNBA
articles.summary: The Valkyries are the greatest expansion experience in sports. From winning games to ignoring trolls, Golden State's first employee explains how the franchis...
articles.body:
Thirty-one months ago, Jess Smith sat at Mission Rock over a plate of petrale sole and outlined an ambitious vision. She was employee No. 1 of Golden State's expansion WNBA franchise, a team without a name, a logo, a color scheme, without a general manager, a coach or a roster. But it was a team with very big plans and dreams.

"We are expecting to be elite," Smith said in March 2024.

The Golden State Valkyries - by now you know their name, their colors, their players, their leaders, their vibe - built a culture, seemingly overnight. Constructed a team that represents the Bay Area perhaps better than any other group. Created a vibe and experience that has become an immediate and indispensable part of the Bay Area sports scene.

Just two seasons into their existence, Smith now oversees a staff of 80. The team has made history in terms of valuation (now at $1 billion), single-season revenue ($100 million) and attendance (selling out every home game it has ever played). The color scheme and merchandise are ubiquitous.

And, in just Year Two, the team is in the WNBA Finals.

"I think the Valkyries are maybe the greatest expansion process that I've ever seen," Warriors coach Steve Kerr said this week. "Everything that they've done, it's been world-class. Like, from Day One. So to see the team in the Finals in the second year is just incredible."

Back when Smith was digging into her sole and mashed potatoes a block from Chase Center, the Bay Area sports world was crowded. The 49ers were weeks removed from a Super Bowl loss. The Warriors were riding the high of their fourth championship, not even two years in the past. The Giants were preparing a stranglehold on Bay Area baseball. A new NWSL team had entered the picture.

But Smith, more responsible than any other single individual for the Valkyries' eye-popping success, had a clear vision. A specific plan. And full confidence that the Valkyries would make something unique and special.

"We've been unapologetic about going big," Smith said this past week. "About being loud. Saying that we're going to be great and inviting people to be part of that with us."

The Valkyries never dreamed small. They never thought about tarping off the upper deck of Chase Center. They never allowed themselves to be dismissed as less-than.

"If you don't believe and go for it, why would anyone around you?" Smith said. "If you're playing it safe, what will the fans you're asking to join do? It does start with vision. It does start with confidence."

Before Smith was hired by Joe Lacob and Peter Guber as the first employee of the new team, she received assurances that this was not going to be a side project. It was not going to be the "little sister" of the "real" Golden State team. She had already built an amazing culture with Angel City, the NWSL team in Los Angeles. She was not interested in joining people who were not fully committed to excellence.

Back in 2024, Smith spoke of "building something that's uniquely our own. Where when someone sees you wearing the brand, you'll be like, 'I get you and you get me.' Where you feel welcome. Something that's inviting and doesn't feel like this is for some people and not for others."

All those aspirational ideas have become reality. The Valkyries have built the most diverse fan base in Bay Area sports; they draw new sports fans, seasoned sports fans, young and old, gay and straight, every ethnicity and race.

"It's exceptional and it's overwhelming," Smith said this past week. "We do have an advantage, and a lot of credit goes to the Bay Area. In this region we love being early adopters. We're not like, 'Prove it and then I'll decide if I want to be involved.' We built around that energy from the very beginning."

The Valkyries' culture came together almost instantly, from the moment Chase opened its doors.

"There is a playbook of a market that's been untapped," Smith said. "That's been waiting for a community like this to come together, to feel connected with humanity at a much deeper level. I think it represents the best of this region and people take a lot of civic pride in what this region is and who we are. Everyone is welcome. Everyone cares about one another. And it's really fun to win basketball games and let out all that energy."

This spectacular culture that the Valkyries have built has managed to keep the team largely immune from the culture wars, the toxic stew of racism, homophobia and misogyny that has bubbled up around the WNBA this season. That is, in part, again, thanks to location. It is also because the Valkyries' experience simply has no room for such nonsense.

"The topic is the beauty of what's happened," Smith said. "What people should be concerned with are these incredible athletes, the communities they represent on and off the court. I feel really proud of what's being talked about with this organization. The beauty of how all these things have come together and what the future looks like. I think that's the league's story, too, and I wish that story was told more conducively and more often.

"We are innately ourselves. I think we are the embodiment of what we think of Bay Area culture. We are concerned with winning but also concerned with one another. I think we (the Bay Area) have always been confusing to the globe in some ways because we can be both things."

Lacob empowered Smith to pursue her vision. He also made it clear he expected a championship within the first five years (which now doesn't seem like a big ask). While he can be a demanding boss, one who has worn out some past employees, Smith embraces his energy and interest, as do her partners in culture creation, general manager Ohemaa Nyanin and coach Natalie Nakase .

"Ohemaa, Natalie and I all have the same energy," Smith said. "Someone just asked me how often I talk to Ohemaa and I said, literally every hour.

"We are all all in, all the time. And Joe is engaged in the same way. It's really beautiful and he has a tremendous amount of pride in what is happening."

It has all happened so fast. But the people who have been building the Valkyries are not as surprised as the rest of the sports world.

"This has been a dream for 2½ years," Smith said. "But if you're around Natalie and Ohemaa and this organization, you realize how incredible these people are as human beings and also at their jobs.

"So a part of me is, 'Of course, I can believe it.'"

articles.title: Kaitlyn Chen is the Valkyries' 'goofy' secret weapon
articles.summary: Chen and the Valkyries start the WNBA Finals on Saturday.
articles.body:
Four days before the Golden State Valkyries ' first WNBA Finals appearance, Kaitlyn Chen was already celebrating, not as a result of some brash overconfidence but out of habit.

Like the other Valks guards, she practiced situational layups and jump shots on a corner court inside the team's Oakland practice facility on Tuesday. Chen then decided to add another element to the drills: a Pete Townshend-style air guitar strum after one of her teammates - Veronica Burton - hit a shot. The energy was infectious, quickly spreading from player to player on the floor and turning this on-court workout into a total party, with each player, regardless of their spot in the rotation, getting a bench mob celebration for their buckets.

For anyone else, this moment could have easily been a fun, spur-of-the-moment thing among teammates. But for Chen, its jovial catalyst, basketball has always been an expression of joy, a common refrain shared by those who have worked with her at all levels. Amid the ebbs and flows of her journey through the sport, the one constant has been how she approaches the game, whether it's been on a team that began as just a backdrop for her education or one where she's a key cog in a championship-bound machine.

Like almost every WNBA player, Chen earned a bevy of accolades in her youth days as she grew up in San Marino, a city just south of Pasadena. At Los Angeles County's Flintridg Prep, she became the program's all-time leading scorer, a four-time Prep League MVP and a three-time All-CIF selection.

Another thing Chen did in high school was catch the attention of Princeton, where she was prepared to commit to playing as early as the spring before her senior year . However, what seemed like a no-doubter briefly turned into a couple of raised questions when the Tigers replaced the coach who recruited Chen with Carla Berube. The new coach, though, immediately got in contact with Chen, spent the summer watching her play AAU games and made enough of a connection for the player to officially commit in September.

In a phone interview with SFGATE on Thursday, Berube shared that it was during those summer months that she first witnessed the basketball joy in person. It wasn't until nearly a year afterward that she'd see it under her tutelage as COVID-19 restrictions canceled what would have been Chen's freshman season. As the campus started to open up some more, Chen worked out alongside Princeton household names like Abby Meyers and Carlie Littlefield. They were tough, but it wasn't enough to wipe away the spark Berube saw in Chen during those previous summer months.

"It was just a lot of two-on-two sessions, or one-on-one sessions, and from that point on, you knew how much she loved the game of basketball and loved being on the team," Berube, who is now the head coach at Northwestern, told SFGATE. "… She brings joy when she's on the bench, and this is on the sideline of practice, too. She's always cheering for her teammates and wants them to be successful and wants to impact them in a way that maybe other teammates don't."

On her way to becoming a three-time Ivy League Tournament Most Outstanding Player, a two-time All-Ivy selection, an Ivy League Player of the Year and a reliable postseason hero, Chen's joyful approach was a foundational part of her basketball experience. Her pregame introduction at one point involved a teammate lifting her up in the air in a direct reference to "The Lion King." She would have lighthearted conversations with teammates during pauses of a game she was actively on the floor for. Berube recalls times during serious huddles where she would call for Chen's attention, only for the guard to look over, smile and wave.

"The goofiness was almost every day," she said with a laugh. "I mean, she does a good job of balancing it, knowing when to be goofy and then also when to lock in and be really focused. There's no other word to describe her other than just really goofy and just fun to be around. I still feel that way. She hasn't changed one bit."

Read our stories ad-free on the new SFGATE app .

After her senior year, Chen still had one year of eligibility left because of the lost COVID season but had to transfer elsewhere to play because of Ivy League rules about graduate participation in sports. It was that very ability to "lock in" that led her to UConn, the most successful women's basketball program in history. Her role went from star-of-the-show, dual-threat floor general in Princeton to experienced and intelligent distributor for stars like Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd. With the dream of competing for a national title, she happily accepted the shift. It was not only what the Huskies needed, as she helped them snap a nine-year championship drought - utterly unheard of in the Geno Auriemma era - but also allowed her to see that she could become a professional player.

Her journey in the WNBA began with an all-time feel-good moment. Chen, who was in the audience on draft night in 2025 to support her teammates, heard her name called 30th overall by the Valkyries, the league's newest team. Over the four-week run from the draft to training camp and the preseason, fan adoration poured in for Chen, and her jersey became one of the most popular in the league.

But it all came to a screeching halt when she checked the training schedule and saw the only thing on there for her was a meeting. She'd been cut, much to the chagrin of many of her new fans.

The Valkyries at least said they'd try to bring her back sometime in 2025. That's when she got to work and began training until the team made good on what it had told her. It seemed like her return would just be a temporary measure, as she was a hardship signing while multiple Golden State players traveled overseas to compete in EuroBasket. But when the roster adjustments happened after the international tournament, Chen remained on the squad. As if to solidify that she was fully on the team, Chen was included in the pregame hype video, just three weeks after her debut.

Even with the debut, Chen needed to lock in one more time. The Valks signed her to a non-guaranteed training camp contract, meaning she once again had to try out for the team that drafted her. This time, cracking the roster would be even tougher . Her hard work, which included special sessions with coach Natalie Nakase alongside Veronica Burton, paid off. She earned her spot on the team, where her on-court skills flourished for a debilitating defensive roster on its way to the finals, and her off-court goofiness flourished as well.

"She can hang out with any single person on this team and bring out the goofy side in them," Burton told ESPN's Andscape . "… I think the world needs to see more of Kaitlyn Chen."

Now, Chen is Golden State's go-to bench guard and spark plug, capable of an offensive explosion - especially from 3-point range , where she's made 43% of her shots in the 2026 regular season and playoffs (34-of-79). She's also a tough, steady presence on defense. But when the world sees Chen on the WNBA's biggest stage over the next two weeks, they won't just see a major role player in this championship-hungry squad, or someone who has worked her tail off at every rung of the ladder she needed to climb to get here. They'll also see basketball joy personified, which has stayed through the ups and downs of her journey.

"There are obviously some bad days and some good days," Chen said Tuesday. "Some days where you love it more, some days when you don't. But I feel like I've been blessed to play with teammates that I love, and that's ultimately what makes basketball so fun for me. It's playing with people that I love and enjoy playing with."

articles.title: Los Angeles Clippers revive ClipperVision for 2026-27 season
articles.summary: Well, there’s at least one good thing about the 2026-2027 NBA season involving the Los Angeles Clippers: ClipperVision is back. The Clippers have had a uniqu...
articles.body:
Well, there's at least one good thing about the 2026-2027 NBA season involving the Los Angeles Clippers: ClipperVision is back.

The Clippers have had a unique stretch over the last year. Between Chris Paul's aborted retirement run, an epic collapse to end the season, a quick playoff exit, the cloud of Pablo Torre's Pulitzer-winning report about Kawhi Leonard's contract, and the NBA dropping the hammer on the franchise because of it, there isn't too much excitement heading into the season.

But at least they made it easier to watch whatever it is the Clippers do this season. The team announced its local television plan earlier this week, with returning ClipperVision broadcasting 77 Clippers games and replacing the now-defunct FanDuel Sports Network SoCal. 10 games will also air on Nexstar's KTLA-5.

In-market fans without a pay TV subscription can stream ClipperVision through a direct subscription, with monthly and full-season pass options.

ClipperVision previously existed as the team's in-market streaming package , but folded into FanDuel Sports Network before the 2025-2026 season.

Like other NBA teams making the best of Main Street's collapse, this is a one-year arrangement. The Clippers expect to join the NBA's centralized media hub in the 2027-2028 season. The deal's financial terms were undisclosed, but SBJ reported that the LA franchise is expected to earn between $16 and $ 18 million in revenue through carriage fees and additional income from a national and local ad partnership with Playfly Sports .

The NBA's new in-house production arm will produce the Clippers broadcasts for an undisclosed fee. Otherwise, the NBA team will return its usual broadcasting team, providing a sense of normalcy in a season that will be anything but. Brian Sieman will be on the call for the 20th season along with game analysts Jim Jackson, Mike Fratello, and Brent Barry, while Ohm Youngmisuk joins as sideline reporter and host.

articles.title: Patna man gets 2 years’ RI for instant triple talaq on wife; acquitted of acid attack charge
articles.summary: PATNA: A Patna court has sentenced a man to two years of rigorous imprisonment for pronouncing instant triple talaq on his wife, according to news agency
articles.body: PATNA: A Patna court has sentenced a man to two years of rigorous imprisonment for pronouncing instant triple talaq on his wife, according to news agency PTI reported on Saturday.Additional District and Sessions Judge Rajiv Ranjan Sahay convicted Naushad Ahmed on Thursday under the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019, and Sections 323 (voluntarily causing hurt) and 341 (wrongful restraint) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).The court also fined Ahmed Rs 6,500. Failure to pay the fine would attract an additional one month and 22 days of imprisonment. However, he was acquitted of the charge of attempting to throw acid on his wife.According to an FIR registered at Phulwari Sharif police station in September 2022, Ahmed, a resident of Simri village, pronounced triple talaq on his wife on September 5 that year. The couple had been married for nearly 21 years and have three children.The woman alleged that Ahmed assaulted her and their children and attempted to throw acid on her. Police filed a chargesheet in the case on July 31, 2023.Speaking to the media, Ahmed’s lawyer, Shekhar Kumar, said the prosecution had failed to establish the acid attack allegation.He also questioned the conviction on the other charges and said Ahmed, who is currently out on bail, would challenge the verdict in the high court.Kumar said the defence was awaiting a copy of the court order. He added that this was the first time a sentence had been handed down in a triple talaq case in Patna district.The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019, makes the pronouncement of instant triple talaq void and illegal and provides for a jail term of up to three years and a fine for the husband.The Lok Sabha passed the bill on July 25, 2019, followed by the Rajya Sabha on July 30. articles.title: 3 things from Charlotte's preseason defeat against Memphis
articles.summary: The Charlotte Hornets fell to the Memphis Grizzlies Friday, ending their preseason with a 1-3 record.
articles.body:
The Charlotte Hornets played their final preseason game Friday night in Memphis against the Grizzlies, looking to improve to 2-2. Unfortunately for Hornets fans, that wouldn't be the case, as the Grizzlies took advantage of Charlotte's mistakes, capitalizing to earn a 19-point victory (117-98).

Recent No. 14 overall pick Hannes Steinbach led the Hornets in scoring off the bench, finishing with 19 points, 10 rebounds and three steals on 7-for-9 shooting from the field. Only three more Hornets players finished in double figures, those being Brandon Miller, Naz Reid and another rookie, Christian Anderson Jr. For Memphis, it was Ty Jerome and Cameron Boozer who set the pace, combining for 36 points, 11 rebounds and seven assists. With Charlotte's preseason now complete, here are three takeaways to take note of as the 2026-27 season nears.

Prior to the game, the Hornets trimmed their roster to 15 players, officially waiving former NBA champion Pat Connaughton. While many believed the final roster spot was a toss-up between Connaughton and Tidjane Salaun, the Frenchman ultimately remained. Still 21 years old, the former No. 4 overall pick has time to prove Charlotte right in their original investment.

With 24 more turnovers Friday against the Grizzlies, the Hornets have now committed 93 in a span of four preseason games. While it is true that Charlotte has been without multiple starters (Coby White and Kon Knueppel), these numbers are concerning to say the least. Against Memphis, the Hornets' starting lineup accounted for 14 of 24 turnovers, with Naz Reid leading the team with five giveaways.

1. Fans should prepare themselves for a slow start

After four preseason games, it feels as though the Hornets still have some things to figure out. Apart from turnovers, chemistry may be the biggest factor. Not only did the Hornets bring in six new players (Reid, Allen, O'Neale, Schroder, Steinbach and Anderson Jr.), but Charlotte has also been without Coby White, Kon Knueppel and Grant Williams for the entire preseason. Considering these factors, it's reasonable to assume that this group will need some time to sync up once the roster becomes fully healthy.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham commends Washington state girls who walked off cross country race over male teammate
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham praised Camas High School girls who walked out of a cross-country race to protest a transgender teammate's switch to girls' competition.
articles.body: WNBA star Sophie Cunningham praised the Washington state high school girls who walked out of a cross-country race in protest of a transgender teammate. "Good work girls," Cunningham wrote in a comment on an XX-XY Athletics Instagram post about the protest. The three-word message echoed her earlier defense of teenage fans caught in a confrontation at a Seattle Storm game after showing support for her stance on women’s sports. RALLY PLANNED TO SUPPORT WASHINGTON GIRLS WHO REFUSED TO RACE AGAINST TRANSGENDER TEAMMATE IN CROSS COUNTRY About a dozen Camas High School runners walked off the course Oct. 13 during a meet against Battle Ground. Their teammate had begun the season competing in boys’ races before switching to girls’ competition. The dispute has drawn national attention and prompted plans for an Oct. 21 rally supporting the runners. Cunningham has previously argued that girls’ and women’s sports should be separated by sex. In a July ESPN profile, she described her position as protecting opportunities for girls while rejecting accusations that she hated transgender people. Later that month, two teenage supporters attended a Fever-Storm game at Seattle’s Climate Pledge Arena wearing XX-XY Athletics shirts and carrying a sign thanking Cunningham for speaking up for girls. The teenagers alleged that Storm co-owner Celeste Keaton confronted them and used profanity. The WNBA subsequently fined Keaton an undisclosed amount and suspended her from attending Seattle’s next five home games. Cunningham then reposted OutKick’s reporting of the Seattle controversy in July, writing "Bravo to those girls for standing up for what they believe," on X. STORM CO-OWNER SUSPENDED AFTER INCIDENT WITH SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM FANS AS STAR BREAKS SILENCE ON CONTROVERSY Cunningham also emphasized that she welcomed people regardless of gender identity and believed disagreement should not prevent kindness. But she sharply criticized the conduct attributed to Keaton. "Truly embarrassing of the co-owner. Unfortunately shows the type of leader she is," Cunningham wrote. Storm majority owner Ginny Gilder apologized for the co-owner’s comments. "Everyone who attends a Storm game deserves to feel welcome," Gilder said in a statement that also reaffirmed the team’s commitment to treating fans respectfully. The Fever said at the time that neither the organization nor Cunningham had advance knowledge of the demonstration held outside the Seattle arena or contact with its organizers. The Camas dispute now brings Cunningham’s support back to Washington as voters prepare to consider Initiative 638 on Nov. 3. The measure would prohibit biologically male students from competing in certain female-only school sports and require health care provider verification of biological sex. Backers say the proposal would protect fair competition. Opponents say it would exclude transgender girls and create new medical and privacy burdens. The Washington Interscholastic Activities Association (WIAA) has said its gender-identity eligibility policy follows state law and that it cannot implement proposed restrictions that would violate that law. Amy Sousa, who helped organize demonstrations supporting Cunningham during the WNBA season, is organizing the "Camas Courage" rally for Oct. 21.
