articles.title: Bronny James, Luka, Austin Reaves' Box Score Stats, Highlights from Lakers vs. Nuggets Preseason
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers closed out the preseason on Friday night with a 121-106 loss to the Denver Nuggets.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers closed out the preseason on Friday night with a 121-106 loss to the Denver Nuggets.

Austin Reaves and Luka Dončić combined for 34 points and five assists, but they also committed 11 of the Lakers' 14 turnovers. Bronny James was held scoreless for the second time in four preseason contests.

As head coach JJ Redick is building up his normal rotation for the regular season, James' playing time has gone down in the past two games. His 12 minutes on Friday night came after he played just 11 against the Golden State Warriors on Tuesday.

It's not a surprise, then, that James' scoreless outings have been in the last two games.

As for the two central figures for the Lakers, it wasn't the best night for either Dončić or Reaves. Both of them are such strong offensive forces, though, that even an off night produces some highlights.

Dončić scored all 15 of his points in the first half, including a three from the logo and a and-one layup over Nikola Jokić.

Reaves, whose 19 points led the Lakers, wasn't going to be outdone by his friend and teammate. He showed off his dribble and handle that left Trevon Brazile with no chance.

There was an incident in the third quarter when Reaves took an elbow to the face from Cameron Johnson. Officials called Johnson for a foul and review led to him being assessed a Flagrant 2, resulting in an ejection.

Reaves remained in the game and appeared to be fine. He made both of his free-throws and a three on the Lakers' ensuing offensive possession.

The Nuggets had seven players score in double figures, including their entire starting five. Nikola Jokić was nearly perfect from the field with 17 points on 7-of-8 shooting, along with eight assists and six rebounds.

Jamal Murray led all scorers with 21 points and had six assists with just one turnover in 31 minutes. DeMar DeRozan's 14 points in 27 minutes against the Lakers matched his scoring output from his previous three preseason appearances.

It's hard to get a full read on what this iteration of the Lakers with Dončić, Reaves and Walker Kessler will look like in the regular season simply because we didn't see them together a lot in the preseason.

James' spot on the roster could be worth monitoring, particularly after Redick mentioned earlier in the week that he has struggled in the preseason. Redick did praise his work throughout the offseason and in practices, so it could simply be a matter of getting him more time with the regular rotation players.

We will find out what Redick's plan for the post-LeBron James version of the Lakers is going to be when they tipoff the regular season on Wednesday against the Warriors at Crypto.com Arena.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown Reacts to 1st Game vs. Celtics Since Trade After LeBron, 76ers Lose Preseason Finale
articles.summary: Friday night marked Jaylen Brown's first time going up against the Boston Celtics in his NBA career following the offseason trade that sent him to the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
Friday night marked Jaylen Brown's first time going up against the Boston Celtics in his NBA career following the offseason trade that sent him to the Philadelphia 76ers.

After dropping 20 points in the Sixers' 125-120 overtime loss in their preseason finale, Brown spoke to reporters about the first game against his former team.

'I played there for 10 years, so it will never be out of the way," Brown said.

"We're not where we want to be yet," Brown said about the 76ers after the loss, "So that's just a part of it. It's a part of coming together, a new group with a bunch of guys, different style, but we just got to keep getting better every day."

This was the second consecutive preseason contest between the two clubs, but Brown didn't play in the Oct. 10 game in Boston. His return to TD Garden won't come until Jan. 21 when the Celtics host Philadelphia.

Boston's decision to trade Brown came after he had the best season of his career in 2025-26.

Taking on a bigger share of the offense with Jayson Tatum out for most of the year rehabbing a torn Achilles, Brown averaged 28.7 points per game, 6.9 rebounds and 5.1 assists per game in 71 starts. He set career-highs in scoring average, assists and tied his career-high in rebounds.

Brown finished sixth in MVP voting, but the Celtics opted to send him to Philadelphia in a package for Paul George, two first-round picks and two second-round picks.

During his tenure in Boston, Brown helped the franchise win the NBA Finals during the 2023-24 season. He was named MVP of both the Eastern Conference Finals and Finals during that run.

Based on how Brown performed in the preseason, he looks to be carrying over his strong play from last year to the Sixers. The 29-year-old averaged 20.0 points on 58.3 percent shooting in three games.

Since the 76ers also have Tyrese Maxey, LeBron James and Joel Embiid, Brown won't have to carry as much of the offensive burden this season as he did in his final year with the Celtics.

Brown will get his first opportunity to play against Boston in a regular-season setting on Nov. 10 when the Sixers host the Celtics at Xfinity Mobile Arena. His first game as a visiting player at TD Garden won't come until Jan. 21.

Philadelphia will tipoff the 2026-27 season on Tuesday against the defending NBA champion New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden.

articles.title: LeBron, Embiid Drop Tell-All Quotes About 'Sacrificing,' What Needs Work After 76ers Lose to Celtics
articles.summary: Having wrapped up their first preseason together, LeBron James and Joel Embiid acknowledged there is still work to do before they become the best versions of themselves for this iteration of the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
Having wrapped up their first preseason together, LeBron James and Joel Embiid acknowledged there is still work to do before they become the best versions of themselves for this iteration of the Philadelphia 76ers.

Following Friday's 125-120 overtime loss to the Boston Celtics, Embiid dismissed the idea "sacrificing" is necessary for anyone on the Sixers in order for them to succeed.

"I'm against the concept of sacrificing," Embiid told reporters . "I think the way I explained it was you do what you do best, and we're going to support you. ... I don't think anybody has to take a back seat."

James emphasized the importance of time and getting everyone in sync since there are multiple new pieces on the team.

"We're getting there," James said . "We're a couple of weeks in. We're still working on our rhythm, working on our kinks. It's not going to be perfect. Obviously, we're just getting together, so it's not going to be perfect. But we've got some things we can build on."

James' comments were echoed by Jaylen Brown, who said the 76ers are "not where we want to be yet" but that's to be expected as they keep learning to play together.

"It's a part of coming together, a new group with a bunch of guys, different style, but we just got to keep getting better every day," Brown added.

Head coach Nick Nurse did use James, Brown, Embiid and Tyrese Maxey more in this game than in the previous three preseason contests. All four of them played at least 25 minutes against the Celtics.

VJ Edgecombe, the other member of the normal starting unit, did not play on Friday night.

The only time all five expected starters were in a preseason game together was against the Brooklyn Nets on Oct. 8. They combined for 59 points of the team's 108 points on 15-of-29 shooting, 16 rebounds and 13 assists.

Much has been made regarding how ball-dominant James, Brown, Embiid and Maxey are, though last season with the Los Angeles Lakers proved James is capable of stepping back to benefit the team.

James specifically used the term " sacrifice " at one point to explain how it helped the Lakers with Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves as their primary offensive engines.

There could be some growing pains along the way, as there have been in the past when James has switched teams. The 2010-11 Miami Heat were 9-8 after 17 games before going on a 12-game winning streak.

The 76ers shouldn't necessarily be expected to recreate that version of the Heat, but they have all the pieces in place to be a dominant team capable of competing for a championship once they figure out how best to play with each other.

We will find out how far along this group is when the Sixers open the regular season on Tuesday against the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden.

articles.title: Angel Reese is in the WNBA Finals, but her Chicago exit raises questions about her winning mentality
articles.summary: Angel Reese addressed her role in the Chicago Sky trade during WNBA Finals media availability, revealing she helped choose Atlanta as her destination.
articles.body: Angel Reese has been talking about taking control of her destiny. With the Atlanta Dream preparing for the WNBA Finals, things have worked out pretty well for her. But OutKick wanted to know what, exactly, she meant by that. Earlier this week, Reese told WSB-TV about "taking control of your destiny" and said, "I wanted to come to Atlanta." Those comments got people talking about how she ended up there, particularly the question of whether she forced her way out of Chicago. ESPN TURNS ANGEL REESE’S 49 ‘MEBOUNDS’ INTO PROOF THAT SHE’S A LEGENDARY WNBA REBOUNDER Accounts sharing the interview clip mocked the defense that Reese never requested a trade and didn’t "run from the grind." There’s a difference between formally asking for a trade and making your dissatisfaction known, and Reese had certainly done the latter. Reese has blocked me on social media, so I’m probably not her first choice for this conversation. I’ve written critically about her and, even more often, her fawning media fans. This was an opportunity to hear her explanation in person. So, during Friday’s WNBA Finals media availability, I asked her directly: "What role did you play in the trade?" "I mean, they..." Reese began before trailing off, looking away, and pausing for about three seconds. "I was being traded," she continued after the false start, turning her eyes back to me. "And I found out I was being traded, and luckily enough, I was able to work with Chicago and where I wanted to go. And Atlanta also wanted me, so it made sense for both of us. And I’m happy just to be here." Watching her answer, it seemed like she was being very cautious about what she wanted to say. She acknowledged helping choose the destination, but began by describing the trade as something happening to her. Chicago went from trading up for Reese to trading her away It still seems strange that the Sky were looking to trade Reese in the first place, given how much Chicago invested in her. The Sky traded up from No. 8 to No. 7 in the 2024 draft to select Reese. The deal included sending Minnesota a 2025 second-round pick and the right to swap first-round picks in 2026. That 2026 pick became an expensive part of the story. In a separate trade the following year, Minnesota acquired Chicago’s first-rounder outright in exchange for the No. 11 pick in the 2025 draft. The Lynx eventually used Chicago’s selection on Olivia Miles, this season’s unanimous Rookie of the Year. Then, after two seasons with Reese, Chicago traded her to Atlanta for first-round picks in 2027 and 2028. The organization went from spending draft capital to make sure it got Reese to deciding it would rather have future picks than keep her. So, what happened in between? Well, for one thing, Reese publicly criticized the roster. "We have to get good players. We have to get great players. That’s a non-negotiable for me," she told the Chicago Tribune in September 2025. ANGEL REESE’S LATEST WNBA CONTROVERSY SHOWS HOW VICTIMHOOD BECAME CENTRAL TO HER BRAND She also said she wanted to spend her career in Chicago, "but if things don’t pan out, obviously I might have to move in a different direction and do what’s best for me." The Sky suspended her for half a game over comments they called "detrimental to the team." Reese said she apologized to her teammates. She never played another game for the Sky, remaining sidelined with a back injury after serving the half-game suspension. Chicago traded her the following April. ESPN’s Alexa Philippou and Kendra Andrews reported when the trade was announced, citing unnamed sources, that Reese hadn’t requested a trade and that there was "no contention" between the two sides. Chicago, according to that account, worked with her representatives to find a new home. That’s a pretty favorable version of events for Reese. And I’ve written plenty about WNBA reporters acting more like PR representatives than journalists, so I’m going to have some questions before accepting that account as the full story. Who were those sources? Were they speaking for Reese, Chicago or someone else? The ESPN report never identified them. How much did that public criticism contribute to Chicago deciding to move on? Reporting that she never formally requested a trade doesn’t answer that. And I’m not taking an anonymously sourced account of an amicable trade as the full explanation for how the relationship ended. Reese’s answer about winning leaves out Chicago Atlanta was quite a landing spot for the 24-year-old forward. The Dream went 30–14 the season before Reese arrived, and she’s helped them reach the Finals this year. Reese had also compared coming to Atlanta with transferring from Maryland to LSU, where she helped win a national championship. So, I asked her a second question: How does she balance looking for a new opportunity to win against staying where she is and trying to build a winner? "I mean, anywhere I go, I’m looking to win," Reese said. "I’ve won at every level I’ve been at. So I know me coming into any situation that I’m coming to, it’s a winning mentality, no matter what it looks like and how long it takes." The Sky weren't strangers to winning before Reese arrived. Chicago made the playoffs five straight seasons from 2019 through 2023, including winning the WNBA championship in 2021. Then the Sky missed the postseason in both of her seasons there. LSU was already winning before Reese arrived Reese also explained why she thought LSU was a useful comparison. "I mean, when I transferred to LSU, not a lot of people expected that we were going to win the championship," she said. "I don’t even know if we were ranked at the time." I checked. They were. LSU finished the season before Reese arrived at 26–6, second in the SEC and No. 9 in the final AP poll. Tigers coach Kim Mulkey had already won national championships at Baylor and had just been named AP National Coach of the Year in her first season at LSU. The Tigers entered Reese’s first season ranked No. 16. The Terrapins went 23–9 and reached the Sweet 16 in Reese’s final season there. Terps coach Brenda Frese was also a national championship coach, but her title came in 2006, 16 years before Reese transferred. Mulkey had won her most recent championship at Baylor in 2019, just three years earlier. Reese explained that Mulkey wanted to push her and prepare her for the next level. "When you have a coach that really believes in you and has a mentality of winning, it really helps," she said. "So I was looking forward to and am grateful for that." FanDuel’s opening-day odds for the 2022–23 season had the Tigers at 50–1, the same price as Maryland. South Carolina was the clear favorite at +135. But you don’t have to join the preseason favorite to improve your situation. Playing for Mulkey at a program coming off 26 wins was a pretty attractive option. articles.title: Hugo González amarga el estreno de LeBron en Filadelfia
articles.standfirst: El español brilla (21+4+3) en el triunfo en la prórroga de los Celtics ante los Sixers (120-125)
articles.summary: El español brilla (21+4+3) en el triunfo en la prórroga de los Celtics ante los Sixers (120-125)
articles.body: La fiesta de LeBron James en Filadelfia acabó teniendo acento español. Hugo González lideró a los Boston Celtics con 21 puntos y fue decisivo en la victoria por 120-125 ante los Sixers, resuelta en la prórroga. El madrileño eclipsó el estreno del Rey ante sus nuevos aficionados y dejó en un segundo plano el primer enfrentamiento de Jaylen Brown contra sus antiguos compañeros. Una noche que debía ser histórica para los Sixers y terminó convertida en una demostración de personalidad del joven español. La expectación fue máxima en el Xfinity Mobile Arena, con 19.746 espectadores entregados a LeBron. A sus 41 años y en su temporada número 24 en la NBA, el alero recibió una ovación atronadora y protagonizó uno de los momentos de la noche con un mate a dos manos tras un pase de Tyrese Maxey. "Es una conexión que tenemos. Una de las mejores cosas que haremos ofensivamente será correr la cancha", explicó James sobre su entendimiento con el base. Hugo González completó su mejor actuación de la pretemporada con 21 puntos, 4 rebotes y 3 asistencias en unos 20 minutos, con 6/10 en tiros de campo y 3/7 en triples, cerrando sus partidos de preparación con 19/30 en tiro y 11/20 desde el triple. Los Celtics, con un quinteto inédito (MCGlothan, DeVries, Cenac Jr., Uzan y Gray) demostraron una enorme mentalidad y no se dejaron intimidar por la diferencia de nombres. Lo puso en valor Hugo González tras el duelo: "Nadie esperaba que ganáramos, sobre todo cuando sacamos ese quinteto y la gente ve quién juega y quién no. Pero no nos importó: salimos a jugar el baloncesto de los Celtics y encontramos la manera de conseguirlo". Una declaración que resume la resistencia de un grupo que remontó 14 puntos de desventaja. El tropiezo también dejó en segundo plano el reencuentro de Jaylen Brown con Boston. El alero, ahora en los Sixers, terminó con 20 puntos y ocho rebotes, pero no pudo impedir la remontada de sus antiguos compañeros. Filadelfia tuvo en Joel Embiid a su principal referente ofensivo, con 27 puntos y ocho rebotes, mientras LeBron se centró en repartir juego y facilitar la adaptación de las estrellas de la franquicia. "Vamos llegando. Llevamos un par de semanas. Seguimos trabajando en nuestro ritmo y en nuestros detalles. No va a ser perfecto; obviamente, nos estamos conociendo, así que no va a ser perfecto. Pero tenemos cosas sobre las que construir", explicó James tras el partido. Su mensaje apunta a un equipo con talento para aspirar a todo, pero que todavía necesita tiempo para consolidar sus automatismos. De momento, la primera gran noche de LeBron en Filadelfia terminó con Hugo González robándole el protagonismo.

articles.title: Who could replace Otega Oweh on two-way contract? Here are 3 candidates
articles.summary: Who could replace Otega Oweh on two-way contract? Here are 3 candidates.
articles.body:
After filling out their roster, the Oklahoma City Thunder could be forced to make another move before Opening Night. Under sad circumstances, unfortunately. Otega Oweh sustained a season-ending torn Achilles tendon in the NBA preseason.

Now that Oweh is out for the entire 2026-27 season, that puts the Thunder in a tough spot. Sure, you liked him enough to add him with the No. 41 pick of the 2026 NBA draft. But surely, you can't keep a two-way spot occupied by someone you know won't log minutes.

If the Thunder eventually waive Oweh, who could replace him on a two-way deal? The other two guys for OKC under that same contract are Brooks Barnhizer and Josh Dix. Let's look at three candidates who could eventually take Oweh's spot on the NBA roster:

This is probably the safest pick. Reading the tea leaves, it seems like the Thunder really like Tilly. He was the first player signed to an Exhibit-10 deal. And so far, he's the only one of the original four who remains on OKC's roster. The other three were waived on Friday.

Tilley went undrafted out of Ohio State in the 2026 NBA draft. He was part of OKC's 2026 Summer League squad. He's a seven-footer who can handle and shoot the ball well for his size. Watch out for him as a realistic option to get a two-way spot.

By a slim margin, Whitehead remains eligible for a two-way spot. He has three years of NBA experience. The 2023 first-round pick is fighting for his basketball dream. Injuries have completely destroyed them. Recently signed by OKC, it seems like the organization likes the talent and is taking a flyer on him.

Whitehead spent two seasons with the Brooklyn Nets. He was on a 10-day contract with the Memphis Grizzlies last year. Before that, he was putting up numbers on the G League's OKC Blue. So there's some history there. If you're looking for headlines, this is the way to go. Most NBA fans know who he is.

Sometimes, you gotta go outside of your bubble. In comes Uzan. He was one of the more decorated guys to go undrafted in the 2026 NBA draft. He should be a familiar name as he spent two collegiate seasons at Oklahoma before transferring to Houston. That's where he broke out. The Cougars have been a national title contender for the last few years. He helped with that.

Right now, Uzan is on the Boston Celtics under an Exhibit-10 deal. But the Thunder can easily swoop in and sign him to a two-way spot. That'd be a cool story as a former Sooner. Plus, he's played well in the preseason. He recently had 14 points in an OT win over the Philadelphia 76ers. And Kelvin Sampson usually has his guys ready to defend at the NBA level.
